We marry technology and innovation with clinical excellence to provide trusted solutions that solve the healthcare industry’s biggest pain points and are on a mission to enable greater access to more convenient, affordable, and effective care.

We do this through our technology-enabled care platform that is designed to help our clients achieve their digital care ambitions – today and in the future. We offer programs spanning the full care continuum, including urgent, acute and specialty care, behavioral health, and services for the treatment of chronic conditions such as heart and cardiometabolic diseases. Programs are powered by Amwell as well as our growing partner network.

For almost two decades, Amwell has proudly served some of the largest and most sophisticated healthcare organizations in the U.S. and worldwide. Our team is passionate about technology’s role in transforming care delivery and making it more equitable, accessible, efficient, cost-effective and navigable for all.

Brief Overview 

This role owns Amwell's marketing web estate and how discoverable it is, across four properties: SilverCloud, business.amwell.com, patients.amwell.com, and LiveHealthOnline. Accountability covers performance and conversion on those properties, the compliance posture of what runs on them, and discoverability as search behavior shifts toward AI-generated answers.

The role directs work rather than performing all of it. Engineering owns development capacity and Design owns visual execution; this role defines, sequences, and holds the quality of the work both produce for the web estate. Page content and messaging remain with the pillar that owns each page, so this role owns the platform and its performance rather than what the pages say.

Core Responsibilities 

What the role owns:

• The four web properties — performance, conversion, and delivery

• Web compliance and governance, including cookie consent and tracking governance

• GEO and AI-answer discoverability across the properties, alongside conventional search performance

• Definition and sequencing of website build and development work delivered by Engineering

• Coordination with the separate Design team on visual work for the estate

• The web roadmap and the case for what it returns

How success is measured:

• Conversion performance across the four properties, and measured improvement in GEO and AI-answer discoverability (primary measurable output)

• Web property performance, including speed and core experience measures

• Tracking-compliance coverage across the estate

• Delivery of the web roadmap against plan

• Contribution of web to demand and engagement funnels

What the role does not own:

Scope boundaries are explicit, so accountability is single-owned and hand-offs are clean.

• Page content and messaging — each pillar owns what its own pages say

• Product application surfaces — Product

• Engineering development capacity itself — Engineering owns the resource; this role directs the work

• Visual design execution — the separate Design team

• Off-site authority and earned citations — Brand and Corporate Marketing with the external agency

• Paid media and demand strategy — Demand Generation Manager

Qualifications

• 7+ years in web, digital marketing, or growth, with direct ownership of a web estate

• A track record of moving a conversion measure on owned properties, not only of shipping site work

• Technical SEO depth, and demonstrated engagement with GEO and AI-answer discoverability

• Experience directing engineering delivery without owning the engineering resource

• Web compliance and tracking governance experience, including consent management

• Analytics fluency sufficient to defend what the web numbers claim

• The ability to hold a roadmap across competing stakeholder demands from multiple pillars

Preferred

• Healthcare or other regulated-industry web experience, including accessibility obligations

• Multi-property or multi-brand estate management

• CMS migration or replatforming experience

• Experience establishing GEO measurement where no baseline existed

Do Well. Live Well. At Amwell. 

Driven by our mission and values, we foster a workplace where Delivering Awesome, being Customer First and operating as One Team aren’t just aspirations – they are how we work, every day.  

Our people are our greatest asset. We strive to empower their growth and development not only as Amwellians but as individuals, through generous total rewards packages, a virtual-first work environment, work-life flexibility, including Summer Fridays and designated Mental Health Days, as well as opportunities to stretch and learn – to name a few. It’s our people who truly differentiate us. Ask anyone and they’ll tell you – you’ll never work with more passionate, more driven and more caring team members.    

We champion a culture of respect and inclusion, accountability and integrity, innovation and collaboration. At Amwell, you’ll do the most meaningful work of your career—improving healthcare for millions, growing alongside incredible teammates, and being valued for who you are.  

Benefits 

  • Flexible Personal Time Off (Vacation time)
  • 401K match
  • Competitive healthcare, dental and vision insurance plans
  • Paid Parental Leave (Maternity and Paternity leave)
  • Employee Stock Purchase Program
  • Free access to Amwell’s Telehealth Services, SilverCloud and The Clinic by Cleveland Clinic’s second opinion program
  • Free Subscription to the Calm App
  • Tuition Assistance Program
  • Pet Insurance 

Salaried, Exempt Roles

The typical base salary range for this position is $121,950 - $149,050.  The actual salary offer will ultimately depend on multiple factors including, but not limited to, knowledge, skills, relevant education, experience, complexity or specialization of talent, and other objective factors.  In addition to base salary, this role may be eligible for an annual bonus based on a combination of company performance and employee performance. Long-term incentive and short-term variable compensation may be offered as part of the compensation package dependent on the role. Some roles may be commission based, in which case the total compensation will be based on a commission, and the above range may not be an accurate representation of total compensation.

Further, the above range is subject to change based on market demands and operational needs and does not constitute a promise of a particular wage or a guarantee of employment. Your recruiter can share more during the hiring process about the specific salary range based on the above factors listed.

Fraud Prevention Notice

As part of Amwell's commitment to maintaining a secure and trusted hiring process, Amwell uses fraud detection capabilities within its hiring platform to help identify potentially suspicious, fraudulent, or unauthorized activity during the recruitment process.

These tools are designed to help protect candidates, Amwell, and the integrity of the hiring process by identifying indicators that may be associated with impersonation, account misuse, or other forms of recruiting fraud. Information generated through fraud detection is reviewed by authorized personnel and is not used as the sole basis for hiring decisions.

Personal information collected or processed in connection with fraud detection will be handled in accordance with applicable data protection laws and Amwell's Applicant Privacy Notice.

Identity Verification Notice

Preferred Qualifications

title: ALM Manager
description:
Headquarters: United States | Remote

About Upstart

At Upstart, we’re united by a mission that matters: to radically reduce the cost and complexity of borrowing for all Americans. Every day, we bring creativity, experimentation, and advanced AI to reshape access to credit, helping millions move forward financially with clarity and confidence.

As the leading AI lending marketplace, we partner with banks and credit unions to expand access to affordable credit through technology that’s both radically intelligent and deeply human. Our platform runs over one million predictions per borrower using more than 3,000 signals, powering smarter, fairer decisions for millions of customers. But the numbers only hint at the impact. Every idea, every voice, and every contribution moves us closer to a world where credit never stands between people and their financial progress.

We’re proudly digital-first, giving most Upstarters the flexibility to do their best work from wherever they thrive, alongside teammates across 80+ cities in the US and Canada. Digital-first doesn’t mean distant. We’re intentional about in-person connection through team onsites, planning sessions, and moments that spark creativity and trust. And whether you choose to work primarily from home or collaborate in-person from one of our offices in Columbus, Austin, the Bay Area, or New York City, you’ll have the support to work in the way that works best for you.

If you’re energized by tackling meaningful problems, excited to innovate with purpose, and motivated by work that truly matters, we’d love to hear from you.

The Team: 

Upstart Bank is a purpose-built, technology-enabled bank that combines innovative lending with disciplined balance sheet and risk management. The Treasury team supports sustainable growth by managing the Bank's funding, liquidity, capital, investment portfolio, and interest rate risk across changing market conditions and economic cycles.

As the ALM Manager, you will own the Bank's first-line asset and liability management and interest rate risk management framework. Reporting to the Bank Treasurer, you will lead implementation and ongoing operation of the Bank's ALM platform, develop and govern key behavioral assumptions, analyze net interest income and economic value sensitivity, and translate model results into balance sheet and risk-management recommendations. You will partner closely with Finance, Risk, Lending, Deposit Product, Accounting, Data, Engineering, and Regulatory Reporting to support a resilient and well-managed balance sheet.

How you’ll make an impact

  • Own the Bank's asset and liability management and interest rate risk measurement framework, including net interest income simulation, economic value of equity sensitivity, repricing gap analysis, and other measures used to assess earnings and capital exposure across changing rate environments.
  • Lead implementation, configuration, and ongoing administration of the Bank's ALM platform, including data mapping and staging, source-to-model reconciliations, model controls, change management, vendor coordination, and issue resolution.
  • Develop, document, and regularly evaluate behavioral and market assumptions, including deposit betas and decay, loan prepayments and curtailments, repricing characteristics, funding rollover behavior, yield curves, and product optionality; perform sensitivity analysis, backtesting, and outcomes analysis.
  • Design and evaluate parallel and non-parallel rate shocks, ramps, curve twists, and business-plan scenarios; identify key drivers of risk, monitor limits and early warning indicators, and explain period-over-period changes in the Bank's interest rate risk profile.
  • Recommend balance sheet, product pricing, funding, investment, and hedging actions to manage interest rate risk within approved appetite and limits, and partner with business leaders to assess the ALM implications of new products and changes in balance sheet strategy.
  • Prepare clear, decision-useful ALM and IRR reporting for the Asset and Liability Committee, executive management, the Board, Internal Audit, and regulators, while supporting policy administration, model risk management, independent validation, examinations, audits, and continuous improvement of Treasury reporting.

Minimum Qualifications 

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business, Mathematics, Statistics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 10+ years of experience in bank treasury, asset and liability management, interest rate risk management, balance sheet management, or a closely related discipline.
  • Experience working within a commercial bank, community bank, or bank holding company and applying bank ALM and interest rate risk concepts in a regulated environment.
  • Hands-on experience operating an ALM platform and producing net interest income and economic value sensitivity analyses under multiple rate and balance sheet scenarios.
  • Experience developing and governing model assumptions, reconciling source data to model inputs, analyzing model results, monitoring policy limits, and preparing ALM or IRR reporting for senior management or an Asset and Liability Committee.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience presenting ALM and interest rate risk analyses to an Asset and Liability Committee, executive management, a Board or Board committee, auditors, and bank regulators.
  • Knowledge of applicable bank regulatory guidance for interest rate risk and model risk management, including OCC, Federal Reserve, and FDIC supervisory expectations.
  • Experience with fixed-rate consumer lending, retail and wholesale deposits, investment securities, derivatives, and the balance sheet dynamics of a de novo or rapidly growing bank.
  • Advanced spreadsheet and financial modeling skills; proficiency with SQL or similar data tools; and familiarity with ALM platforms such as Empyrean, QRM, BancWare, Moody's Analytics, or similar systems.
  • Experience supporting independent model validation, assumption backtesting, model change governance, hedging analysis, or funds transfer pricing; CFA, FRM, or another relevant professional credential is a plus.

Position location This role is available in the following locations: Remote 

Travel requirements As a digital first company, the majority of your work can be accomplished remotely. The majority of our employees can live and work anywhere in the U.S but are encouraged to to still spend high quality time in-person collaborating via regular onsites. The in-person sessions’ cadence varies depending on the team and role; most teams meet once or twice per quarter for 2-4 consecutive days at a time.

title: Analyst
description:
Headquarters: Remote US

At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.

About the Risk & Analytics Team

The Risk & Analytics (R&A) team makes crucial decisions that direct Affirm’s business strategy. We partner with Machine Learning, Product, Engineering, Capital Markets, and Commercial teams to grow Affirm responsibly by optimizing approval, conversion, losses, and profitability.

Operating across the entire customer and merchant lifecycle, we tackle a diverse array of challenges, from optimizing checkout conversion and mitigating fraud risk to building scalable data foundations and enabling international growth. We analyze performance not just to report on it, but to determine where to invest resources for maximum impact through building tools, scalable data infrastructure, and analytical frameworks.

We improve the analytics experience across Affirm by streamlining workflows and fostering a culture of learning and documentation. By taking ownership of the entire analytical lifecycle, from initial question to final business decision, we turn complex data and systems into clear, actionable signals that ensure Affirm grows efficiently and intelligently.

One Role, Multiple Teams

We are hiring multiple Analyst I roles across Affirm's Risk & Analytics organization through this single job posting. Rather than interviewing for one specific team, candidates will go through a shared interview process designed to assess the core skills we look for across R&A.

If selected, we will work with you to determine the best team match based on your interests, experience, strengths, and current business needs. You will have the opportunity to learn more about our teams and share your preferences as you move through the process.

Potential team placements include:

  • Point of Sale (POS): Optimize merchant and checkout performance to improve conversion, approvals, and unit economics across the purchase funnel.
  • Direct to Consumer (DTC) / Card: Drive engagement, repeat usage, and lifecycle health across Affirm's app, web, and card experiences.
  • Fraud: Prevent and reduce fraud losses across the customer journey while maintaining a frictionless user experience.
  • Core Analytics: Build the quantitative research, machine learning models, performance monitoring, and scalable data foundations that enable fast, economically sound decisions.
  • Servicing: Enhance the post-origination customer experience by analyzing repayment behavior, collections strategies, and operational efficiency.
  • International Expansion: Build the measurement and decision foundations needed to sustainably launch and scale Affirm in new global markets.

About the Role

As an Analyst I in Affirm's Risk & Analytics organization, you will join one of several analytical teams working across the customer and merchant lifecycle. While the specific problems you tackle will depend on your eventual team placement, all Analyst I roles share a common foundation: using data to understand business performance, identify opportunities, and help Affirm make better decisions.

You will learn the fundamentals of consumer lending while executing scoped analytical work under the guidance of senior analysts and managers. You will leverage SQL, Python, and modern analytical tools to help optimize business strategies, monitor performance, and turn complex data into actionable insights.

You are a thoughtful, driven individual eager to build a strong technical foundation, learn how to navigate exogenous market changes, and integrate modern AI tooling to solve hard problems efficiently.

What You Will Do

  • Derive Insights & Support Strategy: Leverage data analytics to uncover insights that help optimize product, risk, or growth strategies across geographies.
  • Monitor Portfolio Health: Assist in tracking performance metrics, user behavior, and macroeconomic trends that impact business outcomes, flagging risks and anomalies to senior team members.
  • Technical Execution: Write clean, working SQL and Python to build scalable reporting and partner with Engineering to support the deployment of machine learning and risk models.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with Product, Legal, and Compliance to understand evolving consumer lending regulations and market requirements, assisting in translating them into foundational data models and operational policies.
  • Drive Launch Alignment: Support cross-functional discussions to ensure new product launches and market entries align with our operational capabilities and risk appetite.
  • AI Fluency & Efficiency: Integrate AI tools such as Cursor, Claude Code, and copilots into your daily workflows to accelerate data mining and routine tasks, while carefully verifying outputs.

What We Look For

  • 1–3 years of experience in an analytically driven role. Relevant internships or prior experience in consumer lending, fintech, or the broader financial services industry are highly valued.
  • Degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Engineering, Economics, or a related quantitative field.
  • Solid working knowledge of SQL, Python, or other scripting languages.
  • Familiarity with data mining, data visualization, and foundational statistical modeling.
  • Basic understanding of, or deep curiosity about, consumer lending regulations, fair lending principles, and how machine learning techniques apply to real-world business problems.
  • Exceptional communication skills, humility, and the ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional peers.

Pay Grade - I
Equity Grade - 5

title: Customer Success Manager – High-Touch Onboarding
description:

URL: https://hyros.com/

About the Job

At HYROS, we help businesses understand exactly where their customers and revenue come from through advanced ad tracking and attribution.

We're looking for an experienced Customer Success Manager with 5+ years of experience to own high-touch onboarding and customer success for key customers.

This is not a purely relationship-focused CSM role. Onboarding at HYROS has a strong technical component. You'll need to understand how a customer's marketing and sales ecosystem works, help them connect the right platforms, troubleshoot setup issues, and make sure their tracking is working correctly.

Your goal is clear: help customers get set up correctly, reach value fast, trust their data, and use HYROS to make better business decisions.

This is a high-ownership role. You'll lead customer relationships, identify risks early, solve problems proactively, and be accountable for successful onboarding, adoption, and retention.

What You'll Own & What Success Looks Like

As a Customer Success Manager at HYROS, you'll be responsible for guiding customers through onboarding, helping them get real value from their data, and building strong relationships that support long-term retention.

Your performance will be measured across four key areas:

  1. Customer Retention: The percentage of customers you successfully retain within your assigned portfolio.

  2. Customer Portfolio: The number of customers you manage while maintaining a high standard of service and engagement.

  3. Onboarding & Activation: How effectively you guide customers through technical implementation, complete their setup, and help them start using HYROS.

  4. Customer Satisfaction: The quality of your customer relationships, feedback, and ability to resolve issues proactively.

What Success in This Role Looks Like

First 30 Days — Learning & First Customers

  • Understand HYROS, our onboarding playbooks, internal processes, and customer journey.

  • Become familiar with our tracking technology, integrations, and common implementation challenges.

  • Understand how platforms like Meta Ads, Google Ads, Shopify, CRMs, and payment processors connect with HYROS.

  • Start hosting onboarding calls and guiding your first customers through their setup.

  • Learn how to troubleshoot common tracking, integration, and data validation issues.

First 60 Days — Building Independence

  • Confidently lead onboarding calls and guide customers through technical implementations.

  • Become comfortable helping customers install tracking scripts, configure integrations, validate events, and troubleshoot setup issues.

  • Independently manage your first customer portfolio and keep onboarding progress on track.

  • Identify potential setup or engagement risks early and take action before they become bigger problems.

  • Develop a strong understanding of how customers use HYROS data to improve their advertising decisions.

First 90 Days — Full Ownership

  • Take full ownership of your assigned customers, from onboarding through activation and ongoing adoption.

  • Independently handle most common technical onboarding challenges, knowing when deeper technical support is needed.

  • Run effective customer training sessions and explain complex tracking concepts in a simple, practical way.

  • Help customers understand their attribution data and turn it into actionable business decisions.

  • Proactively manage customer engagement, satisfaction, and retention risks.

  • Maintain strong relationships and consistently positive customer feedback.

First 180 Days — Consistent Performance

  • Independently manage a growing customer portfolio while maintaining a high standard of customer service.

  • Consistently deliver successful onboarding, strong adoption, and positive customer retention.

  • Become a trusted advisor who helps customers make better marketing and business decisions using HYROS.

  • Demonstrate strong technical confidence across common integrations, tracking setups, and troubleshooting scenarios.

  • Identify opportunities to improve onboarding efficiency, customer experience, and retention.

  • Contribute to improving internal playbooks, processes, and best practices.

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years of Customer Success experience, ideally in SaaS.

  • Experience managing high-touch or strategic customers.

  • Strong understanding of customer onboarding, adoption, and retention.

  • Comfort working in technical customer environments. You don't need to be a developer, but technical implementations shouldn't intimidate you.

  • Hands-on familiarity with platforms such as Meta Ads, Google Ads, Shopify, or similar marketing and e-commerce platforms.

  • Comfortable understanding how websites, funnels, tracking scripts, integrations, pixels/events, and customer data connect at a practical level.

  • Able to troubleshoot logically, identify where a setup may be breaking, and clearly explain the solution to a customer.

  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to make complex or technical topics simple.

  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work independently.

  • Comfortable using data and customer signals to prioritize and take action.

  • A proactive, ownership-driven mindset. You don't wait for problems to become escalations.

Big Plus

  • Experience with marketing analytics, paid advertising, ad tracking, attribution, conversion tracking, e-commerce, or technical SaaS products.

  • Experience with platforms and tools such as Meta Ads, Google Ads, Shopify, HubSpot, Intercom, or ChurnZero.

  • Basic familiarity with concepts such as tracking scripts, pixels, events, domains, redirects, webhooks, APIs, UTMs, and CRM integrations.

  • Previous experience managing customer portfolios with a strong focus on retention, customer satisfaction, and long-term adoption.

Why HYROS?

You'll have real ownership over a critical part of the customer journey and a direct impact on onboarding, adoption, retention, and customer success.

You'll work at the intersection of Customer Success, marketing, data, and technology, helping businesses not only implement HYROS correctly but actually use it to make better decisions.

This is an opportunity to work directly with customers, solve meaningful technical challenges, and see the impact of your work on their businesses.

If you're an experienced CSM who enjoys building customer relationships but is also comfortable getting hands-on with technical setups, troubleshooting problems, and understanding how marketing technology works, we'd like to hear from you.

title: Security Software Engineer, IAM
description:
Headquarters: Remote - United States

About Vercel:

Vercel is the agentic infrastructure company, freeing people and agents to ship what's next. For more than a decade we've helped builders move from idea to production with speed, security, and exceptional developer experience.

Now we're scaling our products for both agents and people to ship and run software, built in the open and trusted by OpenAI, PayPal, Ramp, Supreme, and millions of developers worldwide.

About the Role:

Traditional IAM teams operate as an approval queue: a request comes in, someone reviews it, grants it, and (hopefully) remembers to revoke it. Access reviews become quarterly spreadsheet exercises, audit evidence is assembled by hand, and the central team becomes the bottleneck for every decision. That model doesn't scale past a certain point, and Vercel is past it. Adding more approvers doesn't close the gap. Building the system that makes access self-serve, time-bound, and provable does.

This role is about building that system. Identity at Vercel should work like the rest of our infrastructure: defined as code, reviewed in pull requests, deployed through CI, and observable in production. You'll own that transformation end to end: migrating Okta and all related IAM configuration fully behind Terraform, and building the self-serve access platform (including just-in-time access) that lets team and system owners define, request, and time-bound their own access instead of routing every decision through a central team. Provisioning, deprovisioning, and access reviews become workflows the system runs, with the audit evidence for SOC 2 and similar generated as a byproduct rather than a manual scramble.

You'll also own the harder connective work: corporate IAM (employee identity, SaaS access, devices) and production IAM (service accounts, infrastructure permissions, on-call and prod access) usually live in separate silos with separate tools and separate evidence trails. You'll build them as one identity plane.

And identity itself is changing shape. As agents increasingly act on behalf of users and systems, the old model of "one human, one identity" doesn't hold, and there's real debate about how to solve it: carry the human's identity through every hop the agent makes, or give the agent its own scoped identity that never impersonates the user. We don't have a fixed answer yet. We want someone who wants to be in the room helping us decide and then build it.

Because of this, we're optimizing for someone who wants to build identity infrastructure as software, not administer identity products. A software engineer who's gone deep on identity, or an IAM engineer with a strong engineering background, is exactly who we're looking for.

You'll work closely with Security Leadership, located remotely within the United States. If you're based within commuting distance of our SF or NY offices, the role includes in-office anchor days on Monday, Tuesday, and Friday.

What You Will Do:

  • Own the full IAM strategy for corporate, production, and product environments end to end, and own the bridge between corp IAM and product/prod IAM rather than treating them as separate problems
  • Migrate Okta and all related IAM configuration to Terraform, so every identity change is reviewed, tested, and versioned like the rest of our infrastructure, driving infrastructure-as-code adoption and leveling up engineering teams in its use
  • Build self-serve access governance tooling, including JIT (just-in-time) access: design and ship the framework that lets team and system owners define, request, and time-bound their own access, rather than security being a bottleneck for every request
  • Own provisioning, deprovisioning, and access review workflows, built so the evidence trail generates itself and internal and external audits (SOC 2 and similar) are fast, not a manual scramble
  • Work closely with the Accounts team, the engineers who build IAM into Vercel's own product (team and project roles, enterprise SSO, SCIM, API tokens), and find where that world and ours should connect
  • Design and enforce least-privilege access controls across cloud, SaaS, and production infrastructure, partnering with platform and engineering teams to embed IAM early in design rather than bolting it on after
  • Help define what identity and access should look like as agents, not just people, request and hold access at Vercel, and build the first versions of it

About You:

  • 7+ years of experience in identity, access management, or platform security engineering
  • Experience building internal tools or self-service platforms, not just administering existing ones. You'd rather build the framework that lets other teams manage their own access than be the sole approver for every request
  • Proficient in a production language like TypeScript/Node.js, Go, or Python, comfortable designing and consuming REST APIs, and able to ship and operate reliable services. The access platform you'll build is a production system, not a configuration
  • Proficient in Terraform and committed to managing IAM infrastructure as code, ideally with experience migrating existing systems into it
  • Hands-on with identity protocols (OAuth2, OIDC, SAML, SCIM) at the implementation level, not just configuration, including the failure modes: token replay, deprovisioned users retaining access, sync drift between identity providers and downstream systems
  • Experience designing IAM at scale across both corporate (Okta or equivalent: SSO, MFA, lifecycle management, API-driven automation) and production (AWS or GCP IAM: service accounts, roles, workload identity federation) environments
  • A systems thinker who defaults to "why does this class of access request exist" and "how does this scale to the next thousand employees and ten thousand agents," not just resolving the request in front of you
  • Strong collaborator who can drive alignment across Engineering, IT, Compliance, and Security teams
  • Comfortable operating with autonomy and owning decisions in a fast-moving environment

Bonus If You Have

  • Have led a Terraform migration for IAM or identity infrastructure at scale.
  • Have designed or built JIT access systems or an access governance/request platform at a previous company.
  • Have built or managed MDM/MAM tooling (Jamf, Intune, or equivalent) and device-trust integrations with identity.
  • Understand how Vercel's own products handle IAM (team and project roles, enterprise SSO, API tokens) and are excited to partner with the Accounts team to bring internal and product-facing identity closer together.
  • Have a point of view on agent identity (delegation, scoped credentials, impersonation boundaries) and want to help invent the architecture rather than apply an existing playbook.
  • Have experience at a developer tools, infrastructure, or SaaS company.
  • Hold certifications such as Okta Certified Professional/Administrator, AWS Security Specialty, or CISSP. These demonstrate depth, though they're not required.

This role will own regional revenue growth, new-logo acquisition, strategic account development, pipeline health, and forecast accuracy across a complex enterprise territory.

You will lead, coach, and develop a high-performing enterprise sales team while building executive relationships with major digital commerce, payments, and technology organizations. Using a consultative, value-based approach, you will help customers understand how Forter’s Trust Platform can reduce fraud and abuse, improve approval rates, optimize payments, and strengthen the customer experience.

  • Serve as an executive sponsor for strategic opportunities and customer relationships.
  • Represent Forter at relevant industry events, customer meetings, and executive forums.
  • Build a culture of accountability, inclusion, continuous improvement, and customer focus across the regional sales organization.

  • 10+ years of experience in enterprise technology, SaaS, fintech, payments, cybersecurity, fraud prevention, eCommerce, or a closely related market.
  • 3-5 years of experience leading enterprise sales teams, including demonstrated success hiring, coaching, developing, and retaining top sales talent.
  • Proven track record of exceeding revenue and quota objectives in complex enterprise sales environments.
  • Experience managing an Eastern US territory and selling to large, multi-region or Fortune 1000 organizations.
  • Demonstrated success leading complex sales cycles with multiple business, technical, financial, and executive stakeholders.
  • Strong understanding of consultative, value-based, and account-based enterprise selling.
  • Experience with pipeline management, territory planning, forecasting, inspection, and sales performance analytics.
  • Ability to engage credibly with C-level executives and translate complex technology into clear business value.
  • Excellent executive presence, negotiation skills, presentation skills, and written and verbal communication.
  • Strong cross-functional leadership skills and the ability to influence.
  • Experience using Salesforce CRM; strong operational discipline is required.
  • High integrity, sound judgment, resilience, and a passion for developing people.
  • Willingness to travel periodically for customer meetings, team events, and industry activities.

About us:

Digital commerce is built on trust. At every point along the eCommerce journey, businesses must make a critical decision: Can I trust this customer? Answering this simple question accurately and instantly is powerful—it can accelerate revenue growth and strengthen a company’s connection with its customers. How do we do it? Forter was founded on the insight that it's not about what is being purchased, nor where— but who is behind the interaction.

The Forter Decision Engine finds patterns across more than one billion identities in our dataset. We isolate fraudsters and protect customers—ensuring everyone gets the experience they deserve.  Given that trust is central to how we operate, Forter is very much driven by a defined set of values. We attract remarkable talent and have retention and engagement levels that are well above benchmarks. We’re meticulous about strengthening our culture as we grow and ensuring this is an environment where people can have outsized impact. 

Trust is backed by data –  Forter is a recipient of over 10 workplace and innovation awards, including: 

  • Great Place to Work Certification (2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025)
  • Fortune’s Best Workplaces in NYC (2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025)
  • Forbes Cloud 100 (2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025)
  • #3 on Fast Company’s list of “Most Innovative Finance Companies” (2022)
  • Anti-Fraud Solution of the Year at the Payments Awards (2024)
  • SAP Pinnacle Awards “New Partner Application Award” (2023)
  • Fintech Breakthrough Awards – Best Fraud Prevention Platform (2023)

We are a team of over 500 Forterians spread across 3 different continents. Since 2013, we've raised $525 million from investors such as Tiger Global, Bessemer, Sequoia Capital, March Capital and Salesforce Ventures. We're on a mission to bring trust to global digital commerce so that companies like Nordstrom, Priceline, Instacart and ASOS can block fraud, drive revenue and improve customer experience.

title: Director of Security Engineering
description:
Headquarters: Remote - USA

About the Role

Abnormal AI protects organizations from the most sophisticated email and collaboration attacks using behavioral AI. Security is not a bolt-on at Abnormal; it is core to the product we sell and the trust our customers place in us. Our security organization operates a commercial cloud environment and a separate FedRAMP-authorized environment, and we are pursuing increasingly rigorous federal authorizations as we grow.

We are hiring a Director of Security reporting to the CISO and leading the Security Engineering organization. You will build and scale high-performing security teams, own major security programs end to end, and operate autonomously in the CISO's absence, including representing security to executive leadership, customers, and auditors.

This is a role for a deeply technical leader with a software engineering background who has grown into people leadership. You have built security teams from the ground up, you write and review code and architecture when it matters, and you believe the best security organizations earn their influence through partnership rather than policy enforcement.

Our Security Philosophy

We run security the way the best engineering-led companies do:

  • Security reduces toil. Our job is to make the rest of the company faster and safer at the same time. If a control adds friction without reducing risk, it is a defect.
  • Paved paths, safe by default. We invest in guardrails, golden paths, and secure-by-default infrastructure so the easy choice is the secure choice. We prefer preventing classes of problems over chasing individual findings.
  • Partnership over gatekeeping. Security succeeds only through deep collaboration with engineering, IT, and business teams. We embed with builders, we ship alongside them, and we take on their constraints as our own.
  • Engineering-grade rigor. We treat security problems as engineering problems: automated, measurable, code-reviewed, and continuously improved.

If the security cultures that value freedom and responsibility, context over control, and guardrails over gates resonate with you, you will feel at home here.

What You Will Do

  • Serve as deputy to the CISO: act with full authority in the CISO's absence and represent the security organization to executives, customers, and regulators.
  • Lead, coach, and grow managers and senior engineers across Security Engineering and Security Operations.
  • Own the security engineering roadmap: cloud security architecture (AWS-first), detection and response, identity, vulnerability management, and secure-by-default platform investments.
  • Drive cross-functional programs with Engineering, IT, and Product, from AI security governance to data perimeter controls to federal compliance initiatives.
  • Set and defend engineering standards for the security organization: everything as code, automated where possible, measured against outcomes rather than activity.
  • Build hiring pipelines and raise the bar on every hire; own performance management, promotion cases, and succession planning within your teams.
  • Translate technical risk into business terms for the executive team and board, and translate business priorities into a coherent security strategy.

Must Haves

  • 10+ years in security or software engineering, including 4+ years managing security teams, ideally including managers of managers or equivalent scope.
  • A genuine software engineering background: you have shipped production software, and you evaluate security solutions the way an engineer would.
  • A proven record of building and scaling high-performing security teams, with alumni who would work for you again.
  • Deep technical fluency in cloud-native environments: AWS organizations and multi-account governance, Kubernetes, identity and access, detection engineering, and modern SDLC security.
  • Demonstrated cross-functional leadership: you have earned the trust of engineering leaders and shipped security outcomes through their teams, not around them.
  • Strong written communication: you produce decision-ready documents and can drive alignment asynchronously.
  • Executive presence: comfortable presenting to C-level leadership, customers, and auditors without preparation from the CISO.

Strong Signals

  • You are currently a security engineering manager or senior manager at a fintech, high-growth startup, or forward-leaning enterprise, and you are ready for broader scope.
  • You have built paved-path or secure-by-default platforms that measurably reduced both risk and developer friction.
  • Experience with compliance-driven environments (FedRAMP, SOC 2, ISO 27001) without letting compliance define the security program.
  • Experience securing AI/ML systems or governing AI adoption at scale.
  • You have operated in environments where security headcount was scarce and automation was the only way to scale.

Why This Role

You will inherit strong teams, an executive staff that treats security as a first-class function, and a CISO who wants a true partner rather than a lieutenant. The scope is broad, the autonomy is real, and the ceiling on this role is defined by what you take on.

description:

The Head of Design, Development, & Construction will own the entire end to end process of launching new compounding pharmacies nationally. Reporting to the Director of Pharmacy Development & Operations, this role bridges pharmacy operations expertise with construction, facilities engineering, and regulatory compliance to bring new pharmacy sites from concept through licensure and go-live. The ideal candidate has hands-on experience designing and building efficient commercial spaces and pharmacy environments including traditional 503A compounding pharmacies and FDA-registered 503B outsourcing facilities operating under current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP) Standards. Their thorough knowledge enables them to successfully navigate state and federal regulations required for pharmacy facility approval.

At Gilbert Pharmaceuticals , every role is AI-first. Work starts in an LLM to clarify intent and context, moves into the right tools to explore and execute, is tested with real users and stakeholders, and is continuously refined as we learn. We're Looking For

You think outside of the box, excel at creative problem-solving, and are comfortable taking on projects that you have potentially never done before! You are a people-person - empathetic, self-aware, low ego, and extremely positive - and are comfortable working in a small collaborative team where you'll wear many hats. You have care for performance, accessibility, and reliability as part of craft. You are passionate and proficient in written and verbal communication, and comfort pairing with designers, engineers, and marketers.

Key Responsibilities

Acquisition

  • Lead market analysis and site selection to identify viable pharmacy locations nationally.
  • Conduct feasibility assessments and due diligence on prospective sites, evaluating regulatory feasibility, build-out complexity, and operational suitability.
  • Develop and execute entitlement strategy for new pharmacy locations in coordination with legal and operations teams.

Entitlements

  • Lead master plan coordination and manage environmental compliance obligations across all facility projects.
  • Oversee community outreach efforts and represent Gilbert Pharmaceuticals at public hearings as needed.
  • Coordinate regulatory submissions and interface directly with operations team on state Boards of Pharmacy, DEA, FDA, and local authorities for facility inspections and approvals.
  • Develop and maintain a facility compliance playbook for new site design and existing facility modifications.

Design

  • Lead concept and programming strategy for all new pharmacy facilities, translating operational workflows into effective, compliant physical environments.
  • Manage design team selection and coordination, including architects, MEP engineers, and specialty consultants.
  • Lead the architectural design and space planning for new pharmacy locations, including compounding suites, sterile and non-sterile areas, clean rooms, and dispensing environments.
  • Develop detailed facility design standards and specifications aligned with USP <795>, USP <797>, USP <800>, applicable state Board of Pharmacy requirements, and FDA cGMP requirements for 503B outsourcing facilities.
  • Review and approve architectural drawings, construction documents, and engineering plans for all new pharmacy projects.
  • Design scalable production environments for 503A and 503B operations, including batch manufacturing areas, quarantine/release zones, and controlled material flow segregation.
  • Develop HVAC, cleanroom, airflow, and environmental monitoring specifications in coordination with engineering and operating partners.
  • Coordinate with operating partners to ensure facility design supports validated processes, environmental monitoring programs, and batch production controls.

Pre-Con

  • Develop project budgets and oversee value engineering exercises to optimize cost without compromising regulatory or operational standards.
  • Lead GC selection processes, evaluating contractors for pharmacy build-out experience, compliance track record, and execution capability.
  • Manage permit management across all active projects, ensuring timely approvals from local building authorities and regulatory bodies.
  • Develop and track project timelines, procurement schedules, and risk mitigation plans across multiple concurrent site developments.

Construction

  • Serve as Owner's representative throughout construction, maintaining accountability for design intent, budget, and schedule.
  • Provide field oversight through regular site inspections and quality walkthroughs to ensure regulatory and operational standards are met.
  • Maintain rigorous cost control across all active build-outs, managing change orders and contractor performance.
  • Oversee FF&E installation and commissioning of all pharmacy-specific equipment and systems.
  • Manage QA & closeout activities including installation qualifications of critical manufacturing utilities (e.g., WFI systems, clean steam, environmental monitoring) where applicable to 503A and 503B facilities.
  • Drive operational readiness in partnership with pharmacy operations and quality teams, ensuring facilities are inspection-ready as soon as possible.
  • Maintain up-to-date documentation including as-built drawings, equipment lists, and SOPs for all facility environments.
  • Support evaluation of pharmacy partners by assessing the design and regulatory readiness of their existing facilities.

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Architecture, Engineering (Mechanical, Civil, or Chemical), Pharmacy, or a closely related field; advanced degree or licensure preferred.
  • 5+ years of experience designing, building, or commissioning pharmacy facilities, healthcare environments, or regulated laboratory/cleanroom spaces.
  • Ability to understand/learn USP <795>, USP <797>, USP <800>, and applicable state Board of Pharmacy facility requirements.
  • Demonstrated project management experience overseeing construction projects from design through commissioning.
  • Experience interfacing with regulatory agencies on facility approvals and inspections.
  • Proficiency with architectural drawings, construction documents, and facility engineering specifications.
  • Experience designing or supporting sterile manufacturing or 503B outsourcing facilities operating under cGMP environments strongly preferred.
  • Ability to travel to pharmacy sites as needed for construction oversight, inspections, and go-live support.

Preferred

  • Licensed Architect (AIA), Professional Engineer (PE), or Certified Pharmaceutical Industry Professional (CPIP).
  • Familiarity with digital health or telehealth-linked pharmacy models.
  • Strong vendor management experience working with contractors, engineers, and equipment suppliers.

What Success Looks Like (First 12 Months)

  • Documented pharmacy facility design standards and a reusable build-out playbook for new sites.
  • Streamlined project flow to maximize efficiency and completion time per project.
  • Documented budgets for all existing and prospective sites with cost efficient suggestions to scale nationally.
  • Successful delivery of at least three to five new 503A pharmacy facilities on time, on budget, and licensed for operation.
  • Successful delivery of at least one 503B pharmacy facility on time, on budget, and licensed for operation.
  • All existing partner facilities assessed and documented against Gilbert's compliance standards.
  • Strong cross-functional relationships established with pharmacy operations, contracting, and external vendor teams.

What you should bring with you

title: Billing Support Analyst - Philippines
description:
Headquarters: Philippines - remote

At Mixmax, we're building the future of how revenue teams work: smarter, faster, and more human. Our platform helps teams stay on top of every conversation by automating busywork, delivering real-time insights, and integrating with the tools they already use.

We're hiring a Billing Support Analyst in the Philippines to join our small but mighty team as one of the go-to contributors and resources for how our customers are billed. You'll resolve billing questions from start to finish, dig into the technical issues that sit underneath them, and keep our Stripe records accurate to the cent. It's part customer support, part billing operations, and part detective work.

This role reports directly to our Billing Team Lead, who reports into Head of Customer Experience. You'll work closely with Customer Support, Customer Success, Sales and Engineering across global time zones (NAMER, LATAM, EU), and you'll help shape how we use AI and automation to make billing faster and more accurate for customers.

If you check that an invoice's line items add up to its total before you read the customer's email, keep reading.

Outcomes

In your first 3 months

  • Learn Mixmax's plans, pricing, billing policies and Stripe setup well enough to resolve standard billing tickets on your own.
  • Own a share of the billing queue in Intercom (refunds, invoice questions, plan and seat changes, cancellations) with accurate, on-time responses.
  • Troubleshoot the technical side of billing tickets, such as seat assignment, workspace access and plan-status issues, before escalating.
  • Take over daily past-due invoice follow-up and payment-failure handling.
  • Become a reliable backup for the Billing Team Lead, so billing keeps moving when anyone is out.
  • Use AI tools day to day to summarize ticket history, draft replies and check your work, with every number verified by hand, and find new efficiencies for the team.

In your first 6 months

  • Handle complex cases on your own: invoice disputes, proration questions, credits, and billing setup for sales-led contracts.
  • Run recurring reconciliations between Stripe, Salesforce and our product data, and flag mismatches before customers notice them.
  • Write and update billing macros, help-center articles and internal process docs
  • Help test and roll out billing automation, including AI-assisted ticket handling, and define which billing actions should stay with a human.
  • Contribute at least one reusable AI or automation workflow to the team, such as an invoice-dispute triage prompt or a reconciliation checklist.

What you'll own

  • Accurate, timely resolution of customer billing inquiries from first reply to close.
  • Stripe account hygiene: invoices, subscriptions, credits, refunds and payment issues.
  • Past-due invoice collection and failed-payment follow-up.
  • Billing accuracy checks and reconciliations across our systems.
  • Clear documentation of billing processes, so knowledge doesn't live in one person's head

What you'll be doing

  • Answer billing questions in our support queue, explaining charges, proration and plan changes in plain language
  • Diagnose the technical issues behind billing tickets, like a seat that is billed but not in use or a user stuck on the wrong plan, and work with Support and Engineering to fix them
  • Prepare, correct and send invoices; process refunds, credits and cancellations within policy
  • Spot patterns in billing tickets and turn them into fixes, process changes or product feedback
  • Use AI and automation to work faster, while knowing where accuracy, privacy and customer trust require a human
  • Take on ad-hoc analysis and projects that keep billing records correct

What we're looking for

  • 3+ years of combined experience in technical customer support and billing support (invoicing, payments, refunds, collections). You need hands-on experience in both.
  • Experience at a technology or SaaS company
  • Hands-on experience with Stripe and/or accounting and billing software (e.g., QuickBooks, Xero, Chargebee, Zuora, NetSuite)
  • You are very strong with numbers. Proration, percentages, discounts and reconciliations come easily to you, and you check your math without being asked.
  • You are meticulous. You catch the wrong date, the duplicate line and the typo in an email domain.
  • Working knowledge of AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or AI features in support tools). You can explain how you use them, how you check their output, and what you won't put into them.
  • Fluent written and spoken English. You can explain a complicated invoice to a frustrated customer clearly and kindly.
  • Based in the Philippines, with a reliable home setup and a schedule that overlaps North American business hours (we'll agree on it together).
  • Comfortable in a remote, fast-moving organization where processes are still being built and refined.

Nice to have

  • Experience with Intercom, Zendesk or a similar support platform, and with Salesforce
  • Background in accounting, finance or bookkeeping
  • Experience with subscription or usage-based billing models
  • Comfort with spreadsheets beyond the basics (lookups, pivots) or light SQL

Core competencies

  • Numeracy: Fast, accurate reasoning with money, dates and percentages
  • Accuracy & detail: Gets it right the first time and catches what others miss
  • Billing operations: Knows how invoices, subscriptions, proration, refunds and collections actually work
  • ️ Technical troubleshooting: Separates a billing problem from a product problem and finds the root cause
  • AI fluency & judgment: Uses AI to go faster and knows when not to
  • Clear, calm communication: Turns confusing charges into answers customers trust
  • ️ Judgment & integrity: Applies policy fairly, escalates the right things, and treats customer money with care

Why Mixmax?

  • Remote-first with async-friendly workflows and a globally distributed team.
  • A product with strong market fit and a loyal, engaged customer base.
  • A culture that values autonomy, quality, innovation and momentum.
  • Competitive compensation and flexible time off.
  • An inclusive, thoughtful team that values long-term success for customers and for each other.

Our commitment to diversity and inclusion

At Mixmax, we know that nobody's perfect and that no one ever matches 100% of a job description. That's okay. Diversity and inclusion are core to our culture, and we're committed to building a more inclusive and open workplace. No matter your background or how you identify, if you're excited about this role, please apply.

title: Lead QA Engineer
description:
Headquarters: Remote (US)

About the Role

As a Lead QA Engineer, you'll own testing strategy and quality standards across our most important work; Deciding what should be automated, what needs a human eye, where the real risk is hiding, and acting on it. You'll work hands-on across both manual and automated testing, splitting your time based on what a given release actually needs, while mentoring other engineers and acting as the go-to voice on quality across projects. You've got the critical thinking skills to chase down a hard bug yourself, know when to ask for help and delegate, and the range to set direction for how the whole team approaches quality. You seek to help your coworkers and do so regularly.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead test strategy and quality standards across multiple projects, deciding what warrants automated coverage versus focused manual and exploratory testing.
  • Build and maintain automated test suites in Playwright, and use BrowserStack to validate compatibility across browsers, devices, and platforms.
  • Define and run deep manual and exploratory testing on new, ambiguous, or high-change-rate work where automation isn't the right investment yet.
  • Translate requirements into concrete test plans and acceptance criteria, catching gaps in the requirements themselves before they become gaps in the product.
  • Act as the technical point of contact for quality with stakeholders: communicate risk, resolve disagreements about scope, and negotiate realistic testing timelines.
  • Write clear, actionable defect reports in Jira, drive them to resolution, and verify fixes actually hold up under retest rather than just passing a second glance.
  • Use Jira's linking and epic structure to keep testing work traceable, and flag workflow friction in the board with the team before it slows down the SDLC.
  • Mentor other QA engineers in both manual technique and automation practice, including how to write tickets clearly and so well that they need no follow-up clarification, raising the bar on testing across the team, not just on your own projects.
  • Step into any project at any phase to assess its quality risk and recommend a concrete path forward.
  • Stay ahead of testing tools and practices worth adopting, and bring the right ones into real workflows deliberately.
  • Operate and champion the use of AI tooling with an understanding that its output is useful, but not infallible. You treat AI as a tool, not a coworker.

Craft & Leadership Balance

Estimated 60% leadership, 40% craft.

Qualifications

Required

  • 6-8 years of experience in software quality assurance or testing, ideally with exposure to consulting or multi-stakeholder environments.
  • Strong, hands-on experience with Playwright for building and maintaining automated test suites and frameworks.
  • Experience using BrowserStack (or a comparable cross-browser/device testing platform) to validate compatibility across platforms.
  • Deep grounding in manual, exploratory, and regression testing, with the judgment to know when automation is and isn't the right investment.
  • Proven ability to translate ambiguous requirements into concrete, actionable test plans and acceptance criteria.
  • Strong Jira practice: writing tickets so well that no follow-up or clarification is needed, using issue-linking for traceability, and spotting workflow friction before it becomes a team-wide problem.
  • Experience testing across a range of CMS or SaaS platforms rather than a single stack, since our client environments vary and this role needs to move between them.
  • Exceedingly strong communication skills, including presenting technical risk and testing tradeoffs to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. It cannot be stressed enough how important this item is: communication is the whole ballgame.
  • Prior experience as a technical or testing lead on large or multi-phase projects.

Preferred

  • Familiarity with performance testing (e.g. Lighthouse) and accessibility testing (e.g. Axe, WCAG guidelines).
  • Experience integrating automated tests into CI/CD pipelines.
  • Experience with structured test-case formats (e.g. Gherkin) and test case management tooling.
  • A track record of debugging and performance investigation at scale.
  • Creation and implementation of SDLC processes and norms at project and team scales.

Why Current

At Current, we believe the best digital work happens when strategy, design, production, and technology operate as one team. We partner with ambitious brands to create digital experiences that are thoughtful, scalable, and built to drive real impact.

We’re a remote-first agency with teams across the US, working collaboratively across websites, platforms, campaigns, CRM ecosystems, and digital product experiences. Our environment is fast-paced, highly collaborative, and built for people who enjoy solving complex technical challenges alongside smart, supportive teammates.

You’ll have the opportunity to work across a variety of clients and technologies, contribute to meaningful digital experiences, and help shape the future of engineering within a growing agency environment.

The target range of base compensation for this role is $85,000 - $110,000 annually. Actual compensation is influenced by a wide array of factors, including but not limited to skill set, level of experience, and location.

title: Principal Solutions Architect
description:

You know a great technical sale is about more than delivering a polished demo. The real work is understanding what a customer is trying to accomplish, figuring out whether Expel can actually solve it, and making sure what we promise during the sales process is exactly what our teams are prepared to deliver.

As a Principal Solutions Architect at Expel, you'll own the technical side of some of our most complex Enterprise opportunities. You'll lead technical discovery, demonstrate Expel's service, design and drive Proofs of Value (POVs), work through technical objections, and create the bridge between Sales and Delivery so customers aren't starting over once the deal is signed.

You'll need enough technical depth to comfortably navigate conversations across security operations, incident response, SIEM, endpoint, network, and cloud environments. But being the smartest technical person in the room isn't enough. We're looking for someone who can listen, ask great questions, tell a compelling technical story, challenge assumptions when necessary, and build trust with everyone from a SOC analyst to a CISO.

This is a Principal-level individual contributor role. You'll be expected to independently navigate our hardest opportunities, influence people who don't report to you, hold teams accountable when necessary, and help make the broader Solutions Architecture organization better along the way.

Sound like your kind of challenge? We'd like to hear from you.

What Expel can do for you

  • Put you at the center of complex Enterprise security opportunities where your technical judgment can directly influence both the sale and the long-term customer relationship.
  • Give you ownership across the technical sales lifecycle, from discovery and demos through POVs, technical objections, escalations, and the transition into service delivery.
  • Expose you to a wide range of Enterprise security environments across SIEM, endpoint, network, cloud, identity, security operations, and detection and response.
  • Connect you with experienced Account Executives, Sales leaders, SOC analysts, Detection & Response, Product, Engineering, Customer Success, and Service Delivery teams.
  • Give you the autonomy to solve difficult customer problems creatively while maintaining the integrity to be clear about what Expel can and cannot do.
  • Give you the opportunity to influence how we run POVs, approach Enterprise opportunities, transition customers into delivery, and improve the overall Solutions Architecture motion.
  • Let you remain deeply connected to customers and technical work while operating with Principal-level visibility and influence across the business.

What you can do for Expel

  • Own the technical strategy for complex Enterprise opportunities from initial discovery through POV, onboarding, and the customer's first 30 days.
  • Lead POVs end to end by defining meaningful success criteria, building the technical delivery plan, coordinating internal teams, troubleshooting issues, and keeping execution on track.
  • Deeply understand the challenges bringing a prospect to Expel and clearly map those needs to what our service can and cannot solve.
  • Deliver technical service demonstrations and tell a compelling story about how Expel creates security value, adapting your approach based on whether you're speaking with practitioners, executives, or somewhere in between.
  • Act as a trusted technical advisor who can ask difficult questions, challenge assumptions, navigate technical objections, and tell a prospect or salesperson "no" when that's the right answer.
  • Partner closely with Account Executives and regional Sales leadership on opportunity strategy, technical discovery, competitive positioning, RFPs/RFIs, and complex customer requirements.
  • Prepare Delivery teams with the technical context, expectations, risks, environment details, and opportunities necessary for a smooth transition from pre-sales into service delivery.
  • Own technical escalations that arise during POVs or the first 30 days of service, pulling together the right people and staying accountable until the issue reaches resolution.
  • Coordinate across Sales, Product, Engineering, SOC, Detection & Response, Customer Success, and Delivery, influencing and holding stakeholders accountable even when they don't report to you.
  • Maintain strong working knowledge across SIEM, endpoint/EDR, network, cloud, security operations, incident response, attacker behavior, and detection and response.
  • Identify opportunities to improve our POV methodology, technical content, processes, customer handoffs, and internal enablement, then work across teams to actually implement those improvements.
  • Raise the technical and consultative bar for the broader Solutions Architecture team by sharing what you learn and helping others navigate difficult customer and technical situations.

What you should bring with you

  • 8+ years of relevant experience across Solutions Architecture, Sales Engineering, technical security selling, security consulting, security operations, incident response, or similar customer-facing security roles.
  • A track record of operating at a senior or principal level, regardless of your current title. You can independently own complex Enterprise opportunities, influence stakeholders without formal authority, and become the technical person others trust when the answer isn't obvious.
  • Meaningful experience leading complex Enterprise POVs, including technical discovery, defining success criteria, coordinating execution, managing objections, troubleshooting issues, and connecting technical outcomes back to customer goals.
  • Strong security depth with the ability to confidently discuss security operations, incident response, attacker behavior, network architecture, cloud environments, SIEM, endpoint/EDR, and detection and response.
  • The ability to understand how security technologies work together in real customer environments and identify where technology alone doesn't solve the underlying problem.
  • Strong storytelling skills. You can take something technically complicated and make it understandable, relevant, and compelling for a SOC analyst, security engineer, Account Executive, or CISO.
  • Trusted-advisor instincts. You look beyond what a customer initially asks for, uncover what they're actually trying to accomplish, and aren't afraid to respectfully challenge a proposed approach.
  • Strong project and stakeholder management skills with experience coordinating complex work and holding others accountable without relying on formal authority.
  • High EQ and the ability to navigate disagreement, conflicting priorities, and difficult customer conversations without losing trust.
  • Genuine curiosity. You ask thoughtful questions, dig beyond surface-level answers, and continuously invest in understanding security, technology, customers, and the business.
  • Coachability and a low-ego approach to feedback. You don't need to know everything, but you should want to keep getting better.
  • A track record of improving processes, technical strategy, enablement, customer deliverables, or team practices beyond your own individual opportunities.

Bonus points for...

  • Hands-on experience working in a SOC, incident response, threat hunting, detection engineering, or another security operations environment.
  • Experience selling or delivering MDR, MSSP, SIEM, EDR/XDR, cloud security, or other security operations solutions.
  • Experience supporting large Enterprise customers with complex environments, long sales cycles, and multiple technical and executive stakeholders.
  • Experience working directly with Delivery or Customer Success after the sale rather than ending your involvement when the contract is signed.
  • Experience responding to complex Enterprise RFPs and RFIs.
  • Experience improving POV methodology, technical enablement, reusable content, or processes for a broader Solutions Architecture or Sales Engineering organization.
  • A bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Security, or a related discipline.

Additional notes

This role is remote within the United States. While our office is located in Herndon, Virginia, we're open to candidates across the U.S. who can effectively support the customers, Account Executives, and regional stakeholders aligned to their territory.

Travel is expected to be up to 10-20% and may include customer meetings, executive briefings, conferences, roadshows, and visits to Expel HQ.

title: Software Engineer - Query Execution
description:
Headquarters: Portugal - Remote

Be Part of Building the Future

Dremio is the unified lakehouse platform for self-service analytics and AI, serving hundreds of global enterprises, including Maersk, Amazon, Regeneron, NetApp, and S&P Global. Customers rely on Dremio for cloud, hybrid, and on-prem lakehouses to power their data mesh, data warehouse migration, data virtualization, and unified data access use cases. Based on open source technologies, including Apache Iceberg and Apache Arrow, Dremio provides an open lakehouse architecture enabling the fastest time to insight and platform flexibility at a fraction of the cost.  Learn more at www.dremio.com.

About the role
Dremio’s Query Execution team builds the runtime responsible for executing analytical queries at scale. The team sits between query planning and table scans, building the systems that turn query plans into efficient, reliable execution.

As a Software Engineer, you’ll work with experienced engineers to build, test, and support well-scoped improvements to the execution engine. You’ll learn how Dremio’s query runtime works while contributing to areas such as query operators, expression evaluation, memory management, scheduling, and performance.

What you’ll be doing

  • Build and support execution-engine components: Implement, test, debug, and maintain well-defined changes to query operators, expression evaluation, execution scheduling, and resource management.
  • Develop reliable software: Write clear, maintainable Java code; add unit and integration tests; and follow established engineering practices for code review, testing, and documentation.
  • Investigate issues: Help diagnose query correctness, reliability, and performance issues using query profiles, logs, telemetry, benchmarks, and production data.
  • Learn runtime and performance fundamentals: Build familiarity with vectorized processing, concurrency, memory usage, parallelism, data exchange, and disk spilling.
  • Collaborate with the team: Work closely with senior engineers and partner teams to understand requirements, break work into manageable tasks, and deliver incremental improvements.
  • Use AI-assisted development tools: Apply AI tools to code comprehension, debugging, test generation, and documentation, while validating results through testing, review, and sound engineering judgment.
  • Grow your engineering skills: Participate actively in design discussions and code reviews, seek feedback, and steadily take on broader technical responsibility.

What we’re looking for

  • Software engineering foundation: Up to two years of professional software development experience, or equivalent experience through internships, coursework, or substantial personal projects.
  • Programming skills: Proficiency in Java or another object-oriented programming language; willingness to learn and work in a large Java codebase.
  • Computer science fundamentals: Understanding of data structures, algorithms, and basic concurrency concepts.
  • Problem-solving ability: Able to work through well-defined technical problems, ask good questions, and apply feedback to reach a solution.
  • Quality mindset: Commitment to writing tested, maintainable code and learning established development, testing, and review practices.
  • Communication and collaboration: Able to communicate progress, surface blockers early, and work effectively with teammates.
  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

Bonus points if you have

    • Exposure to database internals, query processing, distributed systems, or large-scale data processing.
    • Familiarity with performance-oriented software concepts such as profiling, memory management, concurrency, or vectorized processing.
    • Experience with C++, Apache Arrow, Parquet, Apache Iceberg, Spark, Hadoop, or cloud object stores.
    • Contributions to open-source projects.

Abnormal AI is looking for a Director of Customer Success to lead our Mid Market Customer Success organization. As a member of the Customer Success leadership team, you'll set the strategy and vision for how we engage and retain Mid Market customers across both high-touch and digital motions, building a segmented approach that scales efficiently while still delivering measurable value. You'll partner closely with Product, Engineering, Sales, and the Renewals organization to ensure a seamless customer journey and strong renewal outcomes, and you'll coach a bench of first-line managers to build strong, accountable teams. Must Haves

  • Strong troubleshooting, problem-solving, and root cause analysis skills.
  • Familiarity with cloud monitoring and observability tools such as CloudWatch, Prometheus, or Datadog. 
  • 2+ years of experience working within ITSM and change management processes.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to create and maintain technical documentation.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Computer Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.

Must Have

  • 3+ years of experience in two or more of the following areas:
  • AWS Organizations, Control Tower, and multi-account governance.
  • AWS networking, including VPC, IPAM, WAF, and hybrid network architectures.
  • GitHub Actions, self-hosted runners, or CI/CD platform administration.
  • Cloud observability, infrastructure security, or regulated environments.
  • Implementing cloud controls aligned with SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIST CSF 2.0, or FedRAMP Moderate requirements.
  • Experience using AI-assisted engineering tools, such as GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, or equivalent solutions, to improve development and operational efficiency.
