title: Scaled Customer Success Manager
description:
Headquarters: California
URL: https://www.dropbox.com/

Role Description

As a Scaled Customer Success Manager at Dropbox, you will drive adoption, value realization, and renewal readiness across a portfolio of mid-market and small business managed customers. You will use customer and product signals to identify where engagement can have the greatest impact, then deliver timely, relevant experiences through targeted campaigns, group programs, digital touchpoints, and selective personalized outreach.

You will play a central role in connecting our Programmatic and Digital Customer Success team with the Renewals Desk for scaled segment accounts. You will ensure customer health, sentiment, risk, and adoption signals translate into clear renewal-readiness actions, while identifying and qualifying customer-backed growth opportunities as Customer Success Qualified Leads (CSQLs) for handoff to Sales.

Within the scaled portfolio, you will provide more focused engagement for a priority group of customers and translate customer health, retention, renewal, and growth signals into regular executive-level updates that support forecasting and business decisions. You will also own shared inbound customer channels, ensuring questions and requests are triaged, resolved, or routed to the right partner with clear follow-through.

The successful candidate is a customer-focused operator who is equally comfortable analyzing a portfolio, building repeatable engagement programs, writing clear customer communications, and speaking directly with customers to understand their experience. You will bring recent experience managing or materially influencing customer renewals, including the ability to interpret retention metrics, identify churn and contraction risk, execute save plays, and surface customer-backed growth levers. You will help Dropbox scale Customer Success while retaining the judgment, curiosity, and customer voice that come from real customer conversations.

Responsibilities

  • Own adoption, customer health, and renewal readiness across a scaled customer portfolio, using lifecycle, product usage, engagement, sentiment, and retention signals to prioritize action and improve renewal outcomes.
  • Provide focused engagement for a priority group of customers, partnering closely with Renewal Managers and other account stakeholders to coordinate retention and growth actions and deliver regular executive-level portfolio and forecast updates for top accounts in the scaled portfolio.
  • Design and execute targeted campaigns and scaled touchpoints that help customers adopt key capabilities, realize value, prepare for renewal, and address common risks at the right moments in their journey.
  • Serve as the coordination point between Programmatic and Digital Customer Success and the  Renewals Desk, ensuring timely handoffs, shared visibility, clear ownership, and coordinated save plays for customers with renewal-readiness gaps or identified churn and contraction risk.
  • Own and manage shared inbound customer email channels, triaging questions and requests, coordinating timely responses, and ensuring issues are resolved or routed to the appropriate partner with clear follow-through.
  • Use data to segment customers, identify patterns, test engagement strategies, measure impact, and continuously improve playbooks, content, workflows, and automation.
  • Engage customers directly when a focused 1:1 conversation is needed to validate a signal, understand sentiment, address risk, gather product feedback, or capture a representative customer example.
  • Synthesize customer voice across the portfolio and share actionable insights with Product, Marketing, Sales, Support, and Customer Experience partners to improve the product and customer journey.
  • Partner cross-functionally to operationalize repeatable customer programs, resolve gaps in the customer experience, and identify customer-backed growth levers such as broader adoption, new use cases, license utilization, or additional product fit. Qualify relevant opportunities as Customer Success Qualified Leads (CSQLs) and route them to Sales with clear customer context and supporting signals.

Requirements

  • 4+ years of experience in B2B SaaS Customer Success, Account Management, Digital Customer Success, lifecycle programs, or a comparable post-sale customer role.
  • Recent experience directly managing or materially influencing customer renewals across a book of business, with measurable examples of save plays, churn or contraction mitigation, and retention outcomes.
  • Demonstrated success managing customer outcomes across a broad or high-volume portfolio through a combination of one-to-many programs and targeted 1:1 engagement.
  • Strong analytical judgment and fluency in SaaS retention metrics, including renewal rate, gross revenue retention, net revenue retention, churn, contraction, and expansion, with experience using those measures alongside customer signals to identify risk and growth levers.
  • Experience designing or executing customer lifecycle, adoption, retention, or renewal-readiness campaigns and measuring their impact on customer behavior or business outcomes.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to create clear customer-facing content and lead effective discovery or feedback conversations.
  • Demonstrated ability to coordinate across Customer Success, Renewals, Sales, and other teams, clarify ownership, and move shared retention and growth outcomes forward while managing concurrent programs and changing priorities.
  • Experience with Customer Success platforms, CRM systems, marketing automation, business intelligence tools, or related customer-data systems.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working in a Customer Success model that partners with a centralized Renewals Desk or specialized renewals team.
  • Experience facilitating webinars, office hours, group enablement, customer communities, or other one-to-many programs.
  • Experience applying test-and-learn methods to improve engagement, adoption, retention, or conversion outcomes.
  • Experience supporting collaboration, productivity, content, or AI-enabled SaaS products.

Durable Skills

AI fluency means using these tools to amplify human judgment, not replace it. We believe people with these skills will thrive as work and technology continue to evolve:

  • Awareness: Understand yourself and others.
  • Judgment: Evaluate information and make decisions in complex situations.
  • Adaptability: Learn, adjust, and stay effective through change.
  • Connection: Communicate, collaborate, and build trust.

To learn more about why these skills matter and what the data shows about thriving through change, read this blog post from our Chief People Officer, Melanie Rosenwasser.

Compensation

US Zone 1

This role is not available in Zone 1

US Zone 2

$142,700—$193,100 USD

US Zone 3

$126,800—$171,600 USD

The range(s) listed above is the expected annual salary/OTE (On-Target Earnings) for this role, subject to change. Please note, OTE are for sales roles only.

Salary/OTE is just one component of Dropbox’s total rewards package. All regular employees are also eligible for the corporate bonus program or a sales incentive (target included in OTE) as well as stock in the form of Restricted Stock Units (RSUs).

Dropbox takes a number of factors into account when determining individual starting pay, including job and level they are hired into, location/metropolitan area, skillset, and peer compensation. We target most new hire offers between the minimum up to the middle of the range.

Dropbox uses the zip code of an employee’s remote work location to determine which metropolitan pay range we use. Current US Zone locations are as follows:
  • US Zone 1: San Francisco metro, New York City metro, or Seattle metro
  • US Zone 2: California (outside SF metro), Colorado, Connecticut (outside NYC metro), Delaware, Illinois (Chicago metro), Indiana (Chicago metro), Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan (Chicago metro), New Hampshire, New Jersey (outside NYC metro), New York (outside NYC metro), Oregon, Pennsylvania (D.C. metro), Pennsylvania (outside NYC metro), Texas (Austin metro) Virginia (DC metro), Washington (outside Seattle metro), Washington DC metro, West Virginia (DC metro), Wisconsin (Chicago metro)
  • US Zone 3: All other US locations 

Company Description

Dropbox isn’t just a workplace—it’s a living lab for designing a more enlightened way of working. We’re a global community of bold visionaries and resourceful doers shaping the future of Dropbox and, in turn, the future of work. Our Virtual First model combines the autonomy of a distributed workplace with the power of human connection, creating space for meaningful work and lasting relationships. With a startup mindset and enterprise-level opportunities, we expect Dropbox employees to think critically, stay curious, and use modern tools, including AI, to improve how work gets done. Here, you can be who you are and grow into who you’re meant to be. You own your impact, helping make work more intuitive, joyful, and human for yourself and hundreds of millions of people worldwide. If you’re ready to push boundaries and challenge yourself, Dropbox is ready for you.

Team Description

The Dropbox Customer Experience and Success (CXS) Team shapes how more than 700 million users and 575k teams worldwide interact with our products. We turn insights into actions, bringing empathy and expertise to every touchpoint. Our team embraces resourcefulness and curiosity, pushing boundaries—and ourselves—to improve the customer experience and ensure our customers achieve their desired outcomes with our products, leading to increased customer lifetime value, retention, and growth. Every team member contributes their unique perspective as we collaborate across the organization to amplify the customer voice. If you're passionate about bringing joy, humanity, and simplicity to how people interact with Dropbox, join our Customer Experience and Success team. 

Virtual First

Dropbox’s Virtual First way of working is designed to help people do their best work with flexibility, autonomy, and connection. Day to day, teams work remotely with nonlinear schedules and core collaboration hours that support deep focus and individual working styles. We prioritize asynchronous communication to improve clarity, respect deep work time, and reduce unnecessary meetings. While remote work is the primary experience for our employees, we also prioritize intentional, in-person connection. We bring teams together through regular team gatherings, on-demand workspaces, and Dropbox Neighborhood events in order to strengthen team cohesion, foster creativity, and enhance momentum. Virtual First is built to provide the same access to opportunity, growth, and impact for everyone, regardless of location.

This role requires travel to offsites and various other team gatherings (approximately 5-10% of the year or 2-3 days per quarter). We provide advance notice when possible and encourage candidates to discuss any accommodation needs during the interview process.

AI Fluency

AI fluency is a core part of how we work and grow. It’s not about being an expert—it’s about using these tools thoughtfully and effectively to improve your work and support others. We look for four key behaviors in candidates:
  • Ownership: You use AI responsibly by protecting data, applying sound judgment, and taking accountability for the quality and accuracy of your work.
  • Experimentation: You explore new AI capabilities and apply them to improve workflows within approved tools and practices.
  • Leverage: You use AI to enhance thinking, improve efficiency, and increase your impact and your team’s.
  • Learning: You stay current on emerging AI tools and trends, continuously build your skills, and share what you learn with others.
Together, these behaviors help build a workforce where technology amplifies human judgment, creativity, and impact. Dropbox supports responsible use of AI for preparation, but misrepresentation of skills or experience is not permitted. To learn more, see our approach to AI in hiring.
Dropbox is an equal opportunity employer. We are a welcoming place for everyone, and we do our best to make sure all people feel supported and connected at work.

title: Senior Product Engineer
description:
Headquarters: Novi Sad
URL: https://semaphore.io/

About Semaphore

Semaphore is a remote-first software company building continuous integration and delivery (CI/CD) products for engineering teams. Our customers rely on Semaphore Cloud and our self-hosted enterprise products to build, test, and deliver software securely and reliably.


We have spent years building developer infrastructure at scale. We are now using that foundation to create new products and capabilities for a world in which software is increasingly built by people working with AI coding agents.


About the role

We are looking for a senior product engineer who can take an important idea from an early, ambiguous problem to a useful product running in production.

You will work across product and engineering boundaries: understanding the user, shaping the solution, making technical decisions, building the system, and improving it based on real use. Some work will extend mature Semaphore products. Some will start as a small experiment or a new product. In either case, you will be responsible for getting to a strong outcome, not completing a predefined list of tickets.


AI coding agents are part of our daily engineering workflow. We expect you to use them fluently to explore, build, test, and ship faster. You remain accountable for the work: choosing the right problem, setting direction, making trade-offs, reviewing what is produced, and ensuring that the result is coherent, reliable, and maintainable.


This role is for someone with strong ownership, initiative, taste, and judgment. You should be comfortable moving between product questions, system design, code, infrastructure, and user experience as the work requires.

What you will own

  • Take product ideas from problem definition through design, implementation, rollout, and iteration, including experiments that may grow into standalone products.
  • Work directly with users and internal stakeholders to identify the real problem, decide what is worth building, and make pragmatic scope and architecture decisions.
  • Build across backend services, APIs, infrastructure-facing components, and focused frontend experiences, reusing proven Semaphore systems before introducing new infrastructure.
  • Use AI coding agents effectively while maintaining a high bar for correctness, security, clarity, and product quality.
  • Own the production outcome, including reliability, observability, supportability, and working within Semaphore's security and compliance requirements. Communicate decisions, progress, and risks clearly.

What we are looking for

  • A track record of independently shipping meaningful software products or major product capabilities.
  • Strong product judgment: you can identify the essential user problem, reduce unnecessary scope, and recognize when an experience is good enough to ship—or not good enough yet.
  • Strong engineering judgment across system design, implementation, reliability, and long-term maintainability.
  • Strong backend and systems fundamentals, including APIs, asynchronous processing, service boundaries, state and lifecycle management, retries, idempotency, and failure recovery.
  • Comfort with infrastructure concepts such as virtual machines, storage, networking, authentication, secrets, containers, and cloud platforms.
  • Ability to navigate a polyglot environment. Semaphore systems include Go, Elixir, Ruby, React, and related technologies; expertise in every language is not required.
  • Enough frontend capability to build or extend focused product user experiences without depending on a separate team for every change.
  • Fluency with modern AI-assisted development: decomposing work for agents, supplying useful context, reviewing generated changes, and building verification into the workflow.
    Initiative and persistence. You make progress with incomplete information, surface risks early, and bring in other people when their input will improve the result.
  • Strong written and spoken English and experience working independently in a remote, asynchronous team.


We care more about the quality and ownership of what you have built than a specific number of years, previous title, or exact match with our stack.


Nice to have

  • Experience building developer tools, CI/CD systems, cloud platforms, or infrastructure products.
  • Hands-on experience with distributed systems and event-driven architectures.
  • Experience evolving a mature codebase while introducing a new product or architecture alongside it.
  • Experience in a lean environment where senior engineers participate directly in product discovery and customer conversations.

What success looks like

Within your first three months:

  • You have taken ownership of a meaningful product problem and shipped a useful capability to production.
  • Your work shows good product taste, clear technical decisions, and disciplined scope.
  • You have learned enough of Semaphore's existing platform to reuse its strengths and avoid unnecessary reinvention.
  • You are using AI coding agents to increase your output while keeping the resulting systems understandable, tested, and reliable.
  • Product and engineering decisions move faster because you bring clear options, make sound calls, and follow through.
  • The team trusts you with an ambiguous new product or feature and expects you to drive it to a strong result.

How you will work

This is a senior individual-contributor role with broad ownership. You will work closely with engineering, product, infrastructure, and company leadership. Teams are small, communication is direct, and the person closest to the work is expected to exercise judgment.


You will have room to shape both the product and its implementation. In return, we expect you to take responsibility for the whole outcome: what gets built, why it matters, how well it works, and what happens after it ships.

title: Director of Media Strategy & Activation (Paid Media)
description:

Role Description

Dropbox is looking for a Director of Media to own our total media investment—performance and brand—under a single leader.

This leader will build a unified media strategy that brings performance marketing and brand investments together into one investment thesis and one operating model. They will own the media portfolio end-to-end, from upper-funnel brand campaigns through paid search, paid social, programmatic, mobile, and emerging channels, making investment tradeoffs as business priorities evolve. 

The role also owns how the media organization operates, balancing in-house expertise, agency partnerships, and specialist support to maximize speed, quality, and impact.

The ideal candidate has worked on both sides of the industry—building media expertise at an agency before leading media inside a technology or high-growth company. They understand what great agency partnerships look like while also knowing how to build world-class internal capabilities.

This role sits at the center of Dropbox's growth strategy, connecting brand, performance marketing, Product Growth, Sales, and Marketing Data Science to drive measurable business outcomes.

Responsibilities

  • Unified Media Strategy. Build and own Dropbox's media strategy across brand and performance. Set the annual and quarterly investment thesis, define the channel portfolio, and make the tradeoff decisions on where spend moves and why.

  • Total Budget Ownership. Manage Dropbox's full media investment across paid search, paid social, programmatic, display, video, mobile, affiliate, and brand channels. Own planning, forecasting, pacing, and in-quarter reallocation against efficiency and growth targets.

  • Brand and Performance Integration. Align reach, frequency, creative strategy, and channel mix so brand and performance investment reinforce each other rather than compete. Partner closely with the Brand organization, which owns brand positioning and creative direction, to translate brand strategy into media execution.

  • Operating Model and Partnerships. Design and run the right mix of in-house capability and agency partnership. Own agency relationships, and build the internal muscle where needed.

  • AI-Enabled Media Operations. Develop and execute a point of view on where agentic and AI-enabled workflows belong in the media stack — creative production and testing velocity, audience modeling, budget allocation, bid strategy, reporting, and quality control. Make deliberate decisions about where machine judgment outperforms human judgment, and where it does not.

  • Connect Media to Revenue. Partner with Product Growth, Sales, and Marketing Data Science to connect media signals to downstream outcomes — activation, conversion, product-qualified leads, expansion, and retention. Build the acquisition layer of a unified self-serve and sales-assisted revenue system.

  • Measurement Rigor. Partner with Marketing Data Science on attribution, incrementality testing, and media mix modeling. Be a sophisticated consumer and challenger of measurement methodology, and translate complex performance tradeoffs into crisp, executive-ready recommendations.

  • Team Leadership. Lead and grow a team of channel and brand media leaders. Build clarity on what each person owns, how they are measured, and how their work ladders to revenue.

Requirements

  • 10+ years in media, performance marketing, or digital marketing with increasing scope and leadership responsibility, at a high-growth B2B and/or B2C company
  • 4+ years leading teams, including hiring, coaching, performance management, and org design
  • Deep, hands-on expertise across paid channels — search, paid social, programmatic, display, video, mobile — including planning, forecasting, budget pacing, audience design, and performance management
  • Experience owning brand media alongside performance media, with working knowledge of brand lift measurement, reach and frequency planning, and creative performance optimization
  • Track record managing significant media budgets with clear, demonstrated impact on acquisition efficiency, pipeline, or revenue

Preferred Qualifications

title: EMEA Insights Lead, Consumer and Commercial Strategy
description:
Headquarters: Remote - Germany

Reddit is a community of communities. It’s built on shared interests, passion, and trust, and is home to the most open and authentic conversations on the internet. Every day, Reddit users submit, vote, and comment on the topics they care most about. With 100,000+ active communities and approximately 130 million daily active unique visitors, Reddit is one of the internet’s largest sources of information. For more information, visit www.redditinc.com.

The Global Insights team serves as Reddit’s central hub of knowledge, responsible for translating first-party and third-party data into actionable insights about people, communities, and cultural conversations. The team plays a critical role in helping Sales, B2B Marketing, and Consumer Marketing teams articulate Reddit’s value to advertisers and consumers alike.

Reddit is seeking an EMEA Insights Lead to join our growing Global Insights team. This hybrid role will focus on both commercial and consumer insights, helping advertisers show up more strategically on Reddit while also supporting Reddit’s growth and positioning among consumers across the region.

As the first dedicated Insights hire in Germany, this person will become the definitive voice of Insights across DACH — serving as a trusted advisor and strategic partner to some of the world’s largest brands, agencies, and internal stakeholders. This role combines consumer intelligence, cultural strategy, brand positioning, commercial storytelling, and market expertise to help drive advertiser investment and audience growth across EMEA.

Reporting to the Global Insights Principal, this role will partner cross-functionally with Sales, Marketing, Communications, and Growth teams to shape how Reddit is understood in-market by both advertisers and consumers.

Responsibilities

  • Transform complex first-party and third-party data into persuasive, actionable narratives and strategic recommendations for advertisers and internal stakeholders.
  • Design hypothesis-driven research frameworks that identify the right business questions before selecting methodologies.
  • Conduct and synthesize mixed-methods research, including qualitative and quantitative approaches, to uncover cultural and consumer trends.

Strategy & Growth

  • Translate insights into compelling sales narratives, strategic positioning, and “why Reddit” stories that support advertiser acquisition and revenue growth.
  • Help brands understand how to succeed on Reddit through culturally informed audience and platform insights.
  • Support both advertiser growth and consumer growth initiatives by identifying opportunities to strengthen Reddit’s market position across EMEA.
  • Contribute to brand strategy development, positioning work, perception studies, and Jobs-to-be-Done (JTBD) frameworks.

Cultural Intelligence

  • Surface culturally relevant regional insights that inform marketing, communications, and growth strategies.
  • Develop a nuanced understanding of online communities, subcultures, and evolving social behaviors across fragmented EMEA markets.
  • Act as a subject matter expert on Reddit communities, internet culture, and platform behavior within the German and broader EMEA media landscape.

Storytelling & Thought Leadership

  • Create sharp, provocative, insight-led narratives that challenge conventional thinking and inspire action.
  • Represent Reddit at industry events, client presentations, keynote sessions, and thought leadership opportunities.
  • Influence senior stakeholders through concise, commercially relevant storytelling and strategic recommendations.

Qualifications

  • 7-10+ years experience in consumer and market research, data analysis, consulting, strategy
  • Proven experience working in stakeholder-facing insights, strategy, analytics, or research teams within media owners, agencies, or platform organizations.
  • German and English language proficiency required; French is a plus.
  • Strong presentation and communication skills, with experience representing insights at high-profile consumer, B2B, and client-facing events.
  • Deep expertise in mixed-methodology research, including:
    • Qualitative methods (ethnography, focus groups, moderated and AI-moderated interviews, social listening)
    • Quantitative methods (survey design, segmentation, brand tracking, statistical analysis)
  • Strong understanding of the German media and advertising landscape
  • Ability to engage credibly with senior stakeholders across major German brands and media agencies.
  • Familiarity with platform analytics, first-party data, and syndicated tools such as GWI, Comscore, Ipsos, and survey research platforms.
  • Broad category fluency across key advertiser verticals including CPG, automotive, finance, technology, entertainment, and retail.
  • Working knowledge of the competitive platform landscape across EMEA. 
  • Strong cultural intuition and curiosity around online behavior, digital communities, and emerging social trends across EMEA markets.
  • Comfortable navigating cross-functional priorities and collaborating across multiple internal teams.

Benefits

  • Global Benefit programs that fit your lifestyle, from workspace to professional development to caregiving support
  • Family Planning Support
  • Gender-Affirming Care
  • Mental Health & Coaching Benefits
  • 100% employer-funded retirement savings plan
  • Risk Benefits

title: Engineering Manager, Cloud Engineering
description:
Headquarters: Remote - US

About the Job:

We’re looking for an Engineering Manager to lead LaunchDarkly’s Cloud Engineering team, the team responsible for the foundational infrastructure our products and engineering teams depend on.

Cloud Engineering owns LaunchDarkly’s AWS accounts and networking, multi-region Kubernetes infrastructure, Terraform and GitOps workflows, CockroachDB operations, disaster-recovery capabilities, and FedRAMP infrastructure posture. The team is small, senior, and recently rebuilt. This is a frontline leadership role for a manager who treats operational health as a top priority, leads calmly through incidents, and creates leverage through software, automation, and reliable paved paths.

In your first year, you’ll lead a marquee infrastructure insourcing program from planning through completion. The program’s cost savings will help fund additional team growth, giving you the opportunity to deliver meaningful business impact while strengthening the infrastructure behind LaunchDarkly’s next stage of scale.

This role combines people leadership, operational ownership, and technical judgment. You do not need to be the most senior individual contributor in the room, but you should be comfortable partnering with experienced engineers, guiding tradeoffs, and creating an environment where the team can do its best work.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead and develop a senior Cloud Engineering team, providing clear expectations, coaching, feedback, performance management, and career-development support.
  • Own the operational health of LaunchDarkly’s cloud infrastructure, including incident response, on-call health, service-level objectives, resilience, and disaster recovery.
  • Launch and deliver a multi-quarter infrastructure insourcing program, including sequencing work, managing dependencies, communicating milestones, and ensuring a successful transition.
  • Guide technical priorities and tradeoffs across AWS infrastructure, networking, multi-region Kubernetes, infrastructure as code, GitOps, datastore operations, and compliance-related infrastructure.
  • Build leverage through software, automation, and paved paths that help product engineering teams use infrastructure safely and independently.
  • Support migrations by providing guidance, patterns, and enablement while maintaining clear ownership boundaries with partner teams.
  • Establish team norms for effective AI-assisted engineering and identify opportunities to reduce operational toil through AI and automation.
  • Maintain team health and continuity through change, fostering an inclusive, collaborative, and accountable environment.
  • Partner with Service Frameworks, Core Platform, Revenue Platform, Data Platform, and product engineering teams on shared infrastructure priorities and cross-team dependencies.
  • Communicate roadmaps, operational risks, investment needs, and progress clearly to engineering leadership and cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Participate in hiring and team planning as the organization grows.

Qualifications:

  • 2+ years of experience managing an infrastructure, platform engineering, or site reliability engineering team at a product company, including people management of an on-call team.
  • Demonstrated ownership of incident response, on-call health, and service-level objective frameworks for critical production systems.
  • Experience leading at least one multi-quarter infrastructure migration or insourcing program from planning through completion.
  • Technical fluency with AWS, Kubernetes, and infrastructure-as-code practices, with the judgment to guide discussions and tradeoffs with senior engineers.
  • Experience taking over an established team and maintaining engagement, performance, and retention through a leadership transition.
  • A clear point of view on team norms and practices for AI-assisted engineering.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical and operational priorities to a range of audiences.
  • A thoughtful, calm, and accountable leadership approach, particularly during incidents and periods of change.

Nice to Haves

  • Experience with vendor negotiations or cloud cost management.
  • Experience supporting FedRAMP or other compliance-related infrastructure and operations.
  • Experience operating large-scale datastores or OLAP systems.
  • Experience growing a team through funded expansion.

Pay:

Target pay ranges based on Geographic Zones* for Level M2:

  • Zone 1: San Francisco/Bay Area or NYC Metropolitan Area, Boston, Seattle - $191,800 - $263,670**
  • Zone 2: Irvine, LA, Monterey, Santa Barbara, Santa Rosa, Austin, Portland, Philadelphia, Chicago - $172,600 - $237,270**
  • Zone 3: All other US locations - $163,000 - $224,070**
  • All Zones Inclusive of a 10% Bonus Target

LaunchDarkly operates from a place of high trust and transparency; we are happy to state the pay range for our open roles to best align with your needs. Exact compensation may vary based on skills, experience, and location.

*Within the United States, our geographic pay zones are defined by counties surrounding major metropolitan areas.
**Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), health, vision, and dental insurance, and mental health benefits in addition to salary.

About LaunchDarkly:

Modern software delivery was supposed to be the foundation for a thriving digital business but reality has proven otherwise. Slow, inefficient development cycles, costly outages, and fragmented customer experiences are preventing developers from building their best software. The LaunchDarkly platform helps developers innovate on new features faster while protecting them with a safety valve to instantly rewind when things go wrong. Developers can target product experiences to any customer segment and maximize the business impact of every feature. And by gradually rolling out new application components, they escape nightmare "big-bang" technology migrations. 

The LaunchDarkly platform was built to guide engineers to the next frontier of DevOps by:

  • Improving the velocity and stability of software releases, without the fear of end customer outages
  • Delivering targeted experiences by easily personalizing features to customer cohorts
  • Maximizing the business impact of every feature through the ability to experiment and optimize
  • Coordinating the release and optimization of software to provide consistent experiences across mobile platforms and device types
  • Improving the effectiveness and productivity of engineering teams, by providing insights into engineering cadence and stability

At LaunchDarkly, we believe in the power of teams. We're building a team that is humble, open, collaborative, respectful and kind. Be cautious of emails from other domains.  Legitimate LaunchDarkly recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before making a job offer. title: Senior Infrastructure Engineer
description:
Headquarters: Argentina Remote

Webflow is the agentic web marketing platform for modern marketing teams, helping organizations build, manage, and optimize high-performing web experiences that drive predictable growth and strengthen brand trust. Building at Webflow will need grit, because we move fast, without ever sacrificing craft or quality.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Senior Infrastructure Engineer to improve reliability and stability of Webflow’s customer-facing, production infrastructure, serving millions of page views per hour. Our product is used by over 2 million users world-wide across 190 countries, and you’ll help ensure our platform is secure and scalable for these users as tens of thousands of projects are launched on Webflow each month.

  • Location: Remote-first (Argentina)
  • Permanent, full-time employee (this is not a contractor position)
  • Application Information:
    • Application deadline: applications accepted on an ongoing basis until position is closed and filled
    • This posting is for a new position.

As an Senior Infrastructure Engineer you will:

  • Own and evolve the cloud platform that Webflow's product and engineering teams depend on, including our compute layer, EKS fleet, serverless infrastructure, networking, and cloud operations across AWS and GCP.
  • Help design and maintain our infrastructure-as-code foundation, evolving the patterns and shared components other teams build on.
  • Design and maintain the networking layer that connects Webflow's services, ensuring reliability, security, and scalability across our cloud environments.
  • Help make observability data the foundation of how we operate,  improving the dashboards, alerts, and SLOs for the infrastructure you own so that issues are caught before customers notice, and on-call pages are actionable instead of noisy.
  • Build and maintain AI-powered automation that improves how we manage cloud infrastructure, from policy-as-code and drift detection to LLM-assisted runbook generation.
  • Help define the culture of this growing team as it expands its international presence.

About you 

You’ll thrive as a Senior Infrastructure Engineer if you:

  • Have a background as an infrastructure, site reliability engineer or cloud engineer with an enthusiasm for automation and code, or a background as a software engineer with deep enthusiasm for cloud infrastructure and distributed systems. 
  • Have 5+ years of experience owning and operating cloud infrastructure in a customer-facing environment that allows for little to no downtime.
  • Have deep hands-on experience with AWS and a strong opinion on what good cloud operations look like.
  • Have experience managing Kubernetes clusters at scale, including upgrades, node group management, autoscaling, and cluster add-on lifecycle.
  • Have experience with infrastructure-as-code tools like Pulumi or Terraform, and a strong preference for changes made through code, not consoles.
  • Have experience navigating multi-region or multi-cloud environments on AWS or GCP.
  • Stay curious and open to growth, demonstrating a proactive embrace of AI, and actively building and applying fluency in emerging technologies to elevate how we work, drive faster outcomes, and expand collective impact.

It would be a bonus if you had even one of the following:

  • Experience with Karpenter, cluster autoscaler, or other Kubernetes-native scaling tooling.
  • Have experience with OpenTelemetry, Datadog, Prometheus or Grafana
  • Experience building AI-assisted infrastructure tooling, including cost optimization loops, anomaly detection, or policy-as-code with LLM assistance.
  • Experience contributing to multi-region architecture including data residency, regional failover, or latency-based routing.

You Are:

  • Collaborative: You possess a collaborative spirit, thriving when working with both your immediate team and cross-functional partners.
  • Strategic thinker: You're a strategic thinker, adept at defining clear business needs and evaluating solutions to make informed build-versus-buy decisions.
  • Comfortable with ambiguity: You navigate ambiguous situations with ease, gathering data and making progress even with incomplete information or unclear requirements.

If you don’t meet 100% of the above qualifications, you should still seriously consider applying. Studies show that you can still be considered for a role if you meet just 50% of the role’s requirements.

Our Core Behaviors:

  • Build lasting customer trust. We build trust by taking action that puts customer trust first.
  • Win together. We play to win, and we win as one team. Success at Webflow isn't a solo act.
  • Reinvent ourselves. We don't just improve what exists, we imagine what's possible.
  • Own it all the way. We move fast because the moment demands it, and we hold ourselves accountable to deliver outcomes — for each other, and for customers.

Benefits

  • Ownership in what you help build. Every permanent Webflower receives equity (RSUs) in our growing, privately held company.
  • Health coverage that actually covers you. Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans for full-time employees and their dependents, with Webflow covering most premiums.
  • Support for every stage of family life. 12 weeks of paid parental leave for all parents and 6+ weeks of additional paid leave for birthing parents. Plus inclusive care for family planning, menopause, and midlife transitions.
  • Time off that’s actually off. Flexible vacation, paid holidays, and a sabbatical program to help you recharge and come back inspired.
  • Wellness for the whole you. Access to mental health resources, therapy and coaching.
  • Invest in your future. A 401(k) with 100% employer match (up to $6,000/year) in the U.S., and support for retirement savings globally. 
  • Monthly stipends that flex with your life. Localized support for work and wellness expenses — from Wi-Fi to workouts.
  • Bonus for building together. All full-time, permanent, non-commission employees are eligible for our annual WIN bonus program.

Temporary employees may be eligible for paid holiday and time off, statutory leaves of absence, and company-sponsored medical benefits depending on their Fixed Term Contract and their country/state of employment.

Remote, together

title: Backend Engineer (Multiple Positions)
description:
Headquarters: Remote - US

Backend Engineer

About LaunchDarkly Engineering

LaunchDarkly helps engineering organizations ship software and AI with speed, safety, and control. Our platform gives teams the confidence to release gradually, target experiences to the right audiences, learn through experimentation, understand what is happening in production, and respond quickly when risk appears.

Our engineers build the systems, services, SDKs, developer tools, cloud infrastructure, and product experiences that make this possible. The work spans high-scale distributed systems, reliable data and event pipelines, intuitive enterprise workflows, and AI-powered capabilities that help teams manage the next generation of software delivery.

LaunchDarkly’s SDKs are used in systems that perform trillions of feature flag evaluations each day, giving our engineering work a direct connection to the reliability and customer experience of software around the world. As the company grows, we are expanding beyond traditional feature management into experimentation, observability, and AgentControl—helping customers control more of the software and AI lifecycle. That creates an unusually broad set of technical challenges, visible customer impact, and room for engineers to shape what comes next.

We believe in the power of teams. We work with humility, openness, curiosity, and care; we value clear communication, thoughtful technical judgment, inclusive collaboration, and a strong sense of ownership. We encourage people to apply even when they do not meet every qualification listed below. We are interested in the experience, perspective, and potential you would bring to the role.

About the role

We have multiple backend engineering roles open on various teams. The specific level, scope, and technical focus will be aligned to the opportunity and the candidate’s experience. Experience with cloud platforms, distributed systems, developer tools, SDK engineering, data infrastructure, observability, or AI/agent systems may be relevant for some teams.

As a Backend Engineer at LaunchDarkly, you will design, build, and operate the services that power reliable software delivery for our customers. You may work on APIs, distributed systems, configuration and event pipelines, data services, SDK-related infrastructure, platform capabilities, or backend systems supporting our product experiences.

You will work with experienced engineers, Product, Design, and partner teams to turn customer and business needs into simple, scalable solutions. You will have the opportunity to own work from early design through production, learn from real customer impact, and contribute to systems that operate at meaningful scale.

What you’ll do

  • Design, implement, test, and operate production services and APIs.
  • Lead projects or meaningful components of projects from problem definition through deployment and iteration.
  • Make thoughtful tradeoffs across scalability, performance, reliability, security, maintainability, and delivery speed.
  • Improve the observability and operability of the systems you own, including metrics, logs, traces, alerting, and incident learnings.
  • Collaborate with Product, Design, Support, Customer Success, and other engineering teams to understand needs and deliver useful outcomes.
  • Participate in technical design discussions and code reviews, sharing constructive feedback and learning from teammates.
  • Investigate production issues calmly and help turn operational lessons into lasting improvements.
  • Contribute to a culture of inclusive collaboration, continuous improvement, and high-quality engineering.

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience building and operating production software in a professional environment, or equivalent demonstrable experience.
  • Strong software engineering fundamentals, including data structures, algorithms, testing, debugging, and API design.
  • Experience with a backend language such as Go, Python, Rust, or an equivalent language. (Most of our teams use Go)
  • Experience designing or contributing to services that need to be reliable, observable, and maintainable as usage grows.
  • Ability to explain technical decisions and tradeoffs clearly to both technical and non-technical partners.
  • A collaborative approach and a sense of ownership for both your work and its downstream customer impact.
  • Comfort learning unfamiliar systems and working through ambiguous problems.

Pay:

Target pay ranges based on Geographic Zones* for Level 3:

  • Zone 1: San Francisco/Bay Area or NYC Metropolitan Area, Boston, Seattle - $171,200 - $235,400**
  • Zone 2: Irvine, LA, Monterey, Santa Barbara, Santa Rosa, Austin, Portland, Philadelphia, Chicago - $154,100 - $211,860 **
  • Zone 3: All other US locations - $145,500 - $200,090 **

LaunchDarkly operates from a place of high trust and transparency; we are happy to state the pay range for our open roles to best align with your needs. Exact compensation may vary based on skills, experience, and location.

*Within the United States, our geographic pay zones are defined by counties surrounding major metropolitan areas.
**Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), health, vision, and dental insurance, and mental health benefits in addition to salary.

About LaunchDarkly:

Modern software delivery was supposed to be the foundation for a thriving digital business but reality has proven otherwise. Slow, inefficient development cycles, costly outages, and fragmented customer experiences are preventing developers from building their best software. The LaunchDarkly platform helps developers innovate on new features faster while protecting them with a safety valve to instantly rewind when things go wrong. Developers can target product experiences to any customer segment and maximize the business impact of every feature. And by gradually rolling out new application components, they escape nightmare "big-bang" technology migrations. 

The LaunchDarkly platform was built to guide engineers to the next frontier of DevOps by:

  • Improving the velocity and stability of software releases, without the fear of end customer outages
  • Delivering targeted experiences by easily personalizing features to customer cohorts
  • Maximizing the business impact of every feature through the ability to experiment and optimize
  • Coordinating the release and optimization of software to provide consistent experiences across mobile platforms and device types
  • Improving the effectiveness and productivity of engineering teams, by providing insights into engineering cadence and stability

At LaunchDarkly, we believe in the power of teams. We're building a team that is humble, open, collaborative, respectful and kind. We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. Do you need a disability accommodation?

Fill out this accommodations request form and someone from our People Operations team will contact you for assistance. 

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, LaunchDarkly recruiters will only contact you from @launchdarkly.com email addresses or via LinkedIn from "Verified Recruiter" accounts. Be cautious of emails from other domains.  Legitimate LaunchDarkly recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before making a job offer. LaunchDarkly will never make a job offer without conducting a formal interview process. Our interview process does not involve asking detailed questions by email. title: Senior Developer Educator
description:
Headquarters: San Francisco, CA (Hybrid); U.S. Remote

Webflow is the agentic web marketing platform for modern marketing teams, helping organizations build, manage, and optimize high-performing web experiences that drive predictable growth and strengthen brand trust. Building at Webflow will need grit, because we move fast, without ever sacrificing craft or quality.

We’re looking for a Senior Developer Educator to help us create best-in-class video, written, and hands-on education content for Webflow customers, and those who want to define the next phases of the web. You’ll present on camera as a developer educator, and,  to keep your skills fresh, you’ll build production grade sites using Webflow that we use in our education videos and courses. You’ll also keep your skills fresh by learning how to integrate Webflow with other services and technologies and then develop content demonstrating how.

      • Zone B: $121,500 - $146,000

  • Application Information:

    • This posting is for a new position

  • Reporting to the Director, Education Video

 As a Senior Developer Educator you’ll … 

  • Build the reference websites that anchor Webflow University courses, tutorials, and live training — real, production-quality sites and components that hold up to scrutiny from developers and designers, not just demos that survive a screen recording (see examples in our videos at Webflow University)
  • Shape technical curriculum in partnership with instructional designers and video producers, scoping what each lesson needs to demonstrate and why, before anything gets built or shot
  • Present technical content on camera for tutorials, course lessons, and live sessions — walking through code and craft with the clarity of someone who actually built the thing
  • Work alongside video producers and instructional designers through pre-production, shooting, and review, so what's on screen empowers learners to do the thing
  • Serve as the education team's technical subject matter expert, reviewing content for accuracy and pressure-testing it against how people really work and build
  • Keep the technical library current as the platform ships, deciding what's gone stale, what needs rebuilding, and what's newly worth teaching
  • Partner with product and engineering to understand what's coming, so education is ready when it launches rather than catching up after

  • Proficient in HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with the ability to write, review, and explain code - leveraging AI tools to accelerate development and refine quality.

  • Take feedback on your on-camera work as craft input rather than personal critique
  • Enjoy collaborating with technical and less technical education teammates alike, recognizing the unique role each person plays in the success of a project
  • Are passionate about learning, education, and helping others succeed
  • Are equally confident showing the messy middle of a build or the polished result
  • Stay curious and open to growth — demonstrating a proactive embrace of AI, and actively building and applying fluency in emerging technologies to elevate how we work, drive faster outcomes, and expand collective impact

  • Reinvent ourselves. We don't just improve what exists, we imagine what's possible

title: Software Engineering Manager
description:
Headquarters: Brazil
URL: http://lawnstarter.com

About LawnStarter

LawnStarter is the nation's leading on-demand marketplace for lawn care and related services, with over $150M in annual bookings. We're expanding beyond lawn care to become the one-stop shop for all outdoor home services - pest control, pool cleaning, window cleaning, and more.

About Engineering at LawnStarter

Our engineering team builds the platform that connects hundreds of thousands of homeowners with over 70,000 active service pros. We operate three brands (LawnStarter, Lawn Love, HomeGnome) on shared infrastructure, and we're profitable and growing. Engineering here is fast - we ship constantly, we own our systems end-to-end, and we don't tolerate "not my problem." We have strong processes and existing engineering managers, so you're not building from scratch. You're raising the bar.

The Role

We're growing, and that means adding engineering leadership capacity to support new initiatives. You'll lead cross-functional delivery teams of 4-5 engineers, reporting to our Head of Engineering. Your job is to make sure your team ships reliably, grows professionally, and doesn't become a bottleneck as LawnStarter scales into new service verticals.

This is a people-first role. If your identity as an EM is primarily technical - if you'd rather review architecture than develop an underperformer - this isn't the right fit. If you're the manager who knows what every person on your team needs to grow, who handles conflict directly, and who can articulate team performance in metrics, keep reading.

What makes this role different:

- You'll own both delivery AND people outcomes - neither can be delegated

- Distributed team across time zones, so async leadership and written communication matter as much as meetings

- We move fast and actually ship - you'll feel the difference between a team that's humming and one that's stuck

- AI-forward is not a buzzword here - we expect you to lead your team on how to use it, not just follow along

What You'll Own

- People development: Concrete growth plans for every IC on your team - not just the struggling ones. You know where each person is going and what it takes to get there.

- Delivery: Your team ships on cadence with predictable quality. You surface risk early, manage scope, and don't miss commitments without warning.

- Team health: Conflict gets addressed directly. Underperformers are managed with a clear process. Top performers are protected and developed.

- Cross-functional partnership: You're the interface between your team and Product, Design, and other engineering teams. Decisions get made, not stalled.

- Technical direction: Close enough to the work to weigh in on system design and catch architectural risks. Not so close that you're in the weeds instead of removing blockers.

- AI adoption: You're actively introducing AI tools and workflows into how your team operates - code review, documentation, sprint planning, debugging. You set the pace, not follow it.

Problems to Solve

Building people leadership depth as the team scales

LawnStarter is expanding into new service verticals quickly. That means new headcount, new complexity, and more pressure on EMs to develop the next generation of senior engineers and tech leads - not just ship features. We need an EM who's done this before, not one who's figuring it out.

Managing distributed teams without losing culture or accountability

Our engineering team spans multiple time zones and countries. Async communication, remote 1:1s, and distributed sprint ceremonies are the norm - not a workaround. An EM who needs daily in-person proximity to lead effectively won't thrive here.

Turning delivery consistency into a competitive advantage

We have product-market fit and real momentum. The constraint now is shipping reliably enough to compound on that momentum. Your team's velocity and predictability directly affects LawnStarter's ability to launch new services and capture market share.

Orchestrating cross-functional delivery from roadmap to release

An EM here is the connective tissue between Product, Design, and specialist functions - quality engineering, architecture, and security - from estimation through delivery. The hard part isn't running any one of those conversations well; it's running all of them in parallel without becoming the bottleneck they route through. We need an EM who can hold business value and technical soundness in view at once and make the tradeoff calls - not one who stalls when Product wants speed, Security wants rigor, and Architecture wants the durable answer.

Turning AI adoption into throughput without sacrificing craftsmanship

We're not experimenting with AI on the margins. Claude Code, spec-driven development, and AI-assisted review are becoming default workflows here - and we track adoption seriously. We need an EM who can turn "the team uses AI" into measurable throughput without letting quality slip, with real opinions about where AI helps and where it quietly creates debt.

What Success Looks Like (Year 1)

- Every engineer on your team has a documented growth plan within 60 days - and you can speak to it from memory

- Your team ships its committed scope on cadence within 90 days

- Zero surprise departures - you know your retention risks and are actively working them

- Underperformance is addressed directly and documented, not deferred

- The Head of Engineering trusts your team's commitments because you've proven they're reliable

- Your team is visibly more AI-enabled than when you joined - new tools adopted, old manual tasks automated, engineers unblocked faster

Requirements

Who You Are

Deeply AI-integrated, not just AI-aware. You've gone well past "I use ChatGPT to write emails." Your engineers expect you to bring new AI workflows to the team - you've used Claude to accelerate code review, built prompts that help engineers write sharper tickets, or led your team's adoption of Copilot in the development workflow. When you see a task eating team time, your first instinct is to figure out if AI can handle it. You're actively experimenting, sharing what works, and setting the pace on AI adoption for your team - not following someone else's lead. This is unlikely to be a good fit if your AI usage stops at occasional prompting, if you're still evaluating whether the tools are worth the learning curve, or if you'd describe yourself as "AI-curious" rather than AI-native.

A people developer, not just a delivery manager. You can give concrete examples of career growth plans you've built, hard conversations you've had, and underperformers you've managed through a structured process. You spend your 1:1 time on people, not status updates. This is unlikely to be a good fit if your management examples are mostly about process improvements or shipping milestones - or if you tend to blame team outcomes on the engineers rather than the environment you built.

Remote-native. You've led full-remote teams before - not just as a workaround during COVID, but as a default. You know how to build trust without shared physical space, how to run async decision-making, and how to keep distributed engineers from feeling isolated. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you haven't managed a fully remote team in a leadership position, or if you feel like remote work is harder than in-person management.

Direct in conflict. When there's tension on the team - between engineers, between engineering and product, between a team member's performance and what's expected - you address it directly and quickly. You don't let it simmer. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you've left roles or situations because of unresolved conflict, or if your conflict resolution examples are mostly about "creating space for dialogue" without resolution.

Data-driven about people and delivery. You can articulate your team's performance in metrics - not just vibes. You track velocity, retention risk, and IC growth, and you use that data to make decisions. This is unlikely to be a good fit if your answers to performance questions are mostly common-sense observations without examples tied to specific numbers or outcomes.

Technically credible. You stay close enough to the code to earn your engineers' respect - code reviews, architectural input, helping debug under pressure. You don't need to be the best engineer in the room, but your team needs to believe you understand what they're doing. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you've fully transitioned to pure management and haven't touched technical work in years.

A delegator, not a bottleneck. Your job is to build a team that makes good decisions without you - not to be the person all decisions flow through. You coach engineers toward answers rather than providing them. When you go hands-on, it's deliberate and time-bounded, not a default. This is unlikely to be a good fit if your instinct when a team struggles is to take over, if you find yourself becoming the access point for all requests, or if your team's output goes down when you're unavailable.

This Role Is NOT

- A pure technical architect role. The team has senior engineers. Your job is to make sure they're effective and growing, not to be the smartest person in every technical conversation.

- A process manager. We have processes. Your job isn't to document them better - it's to lead the people running them and improve outcomes.

- A stepping stone. We're looking for someone committed to people leadership as their primary craft - not someone who's considering moving back to IC or is ambivalent about managing people vs. building systems.

- A reactive firefighter. We want someone who surfaces risk early and manages it proactively - not someone who thrives in chaos and sees every crisis as a badge of honor.

- An AI skeptic in a leadership seat. We expect our engineering leaders to actively drive AI adoption on their teams, not wait to be convinced.

Benefits

- Rate: $120,000-$140,000 USD annually (contractor), depending on experience

- Location: Fully remote - this role is built for remote-first leaders

- Flexibility: Structured work hours with reasonable flexibility for life

LawnStarter provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, or genetics. We comply with applicable state and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment.

title: Senior Support Engineer
description:

URL: https://townweb.com

Senior Support Engineer

Town Web · HeyGov · ClerkMinutes. Remote, Central US hours. $85,000 to $105,000 a year. Open to candidates in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and Ireland.

About us

We make municipal software built for clerks: websites residents can use, forms and payments that replace stacks of paper, and meeting minutes drafted after every meeting. More than 1,300 local governments rely on us, from counties and cities to villages and towns. We have local government clients in almost every state in the U.S.

Our clients are municipal clerks and the government teams around them. They keep city hall running and rarely get thanked for it. Your job is to make working with us the easy part of their week.

The role

This is the senior seat on our Client Success team. We are hiring you to raise the standard of our support: fix what is broken, write down how it should work, and show what great looks like.

Our AI agent now answers repeatable, well-documented questions. What is left is the work that only a person can do: own a client's problem from the first message to the confirmed fix, build a relationship a clerk trusts, and turn what you learn into better documentation and a better product.

This is not a ticket-closing job. Think of a great 5-star hotel that puts slippers by the bed before you ask. We want a clerk to finish a conversation with you and tell the clerk in the next town about the great experience they had. If that takes three calls, take three calls.

It is also a technical job. You will work with our developers every day. When something breaks, you work out where it lives before anyone else has to. Is the problem on the events calendar on the client's homepage, or in the calendar widget embedded on a department page? Is the wrong speaker name only in the transcript, or is it also in the finished minutes? You reproduce it, write it up so a developer can act without a follow-up question, stay on it until it ships, and tell the client yourself.

You need both halves. A brilliant troubleshooter who is short with a clerk will not work here. Neither will a lovely person who forwards every problem to a developer.

Your first 90 days

  • Learn all of our products well enough to teach them
  • Take over every open escalation and close or schedule each one
  • Rebuild the path from support to our developers so nothing leaves the queue untracked
  • Find the ten questions clerks ask most and fix each at the source: an article, a Fin answer, or a product change

What you will do

Raise the standard

  • Design how issues move from support to developers, and keep that path working
  • Set the bar for replies, calls, and write-ups, and coach teammates by example
  • Turn what you fix into playbooks the team and Fin can follow

Delight clients

  • Make every interaction feel personal, warm, and unhurried, especially for less technical users who would rather talk to a person than read a help article
  • Step in when the AI agent or the documentation is not enough, and make sure the client feels heard and helped, not processed
  • Treat client sentiment as the real measure of success, not ticket speed
  • Look for small moments to go above and beyond, and share what works so it becomes how the whole team operates

Own the problem from start to finish

  • Be the named person on an account when things go wrong: one owner, one plan, regular updates, until the client says it is fixed
  • Step in early when an account shows strain (repeat tickets, a rough launch, a frustrated message) and run the recovery. Get on a call, write down what is open, set dates, follow through
  • Make sure nothing sits untracked once it leaves the support queue

Diagnose, then escalate

  • Work out which product and which layer an issue lives in before you hand it to a developer
  • Reproduce it, capture the steps with screenshots or a recording, and file it in Linear with everything a developer needs
  • Check on your open Linear issues, chase what is stuck, and confirm the fix with the client
  • Use Claude, connected to our code repository, to trace where a behavior comes from. For small, well-understood fixes, draft the change for a developer to review

Knowledge base and AI support

  • Inherit and maintain the help center for all of our products. It is what our AI agent (Fin, in Intercom) answers from
  • Write and improve articles from real, recurring questions, on a weekly rhythm measured against live ticket volume
  • Write troubleshooting guides that separate look-alike problems, so the next person, or Fin, can tell them apart
  • Tune Fin: review where it failed, fix the article, and teach it to ask a clarifying question when a request could mean two things
  • Record short training videos so clients can learn at their own pace

Support and onboarding

  • Handle the conversations Fin cannot resolve across Town Web (websites), HeyGov (forms, payments, reservations, campaigns), and ClerkMinutes (agendas, transcripts, minutes)
  • Help new clients through onboarding with the projects team so they reach value quickly
  • Talk with clerks by phone and video every week. Get on a call whenever a situation needs a human voice

Account care

  • Build real relationships with your assigned accounts
  • Understand what each client is trying to accomplish, what they use, what they do not know we offer, and where they will need help before they ask
  • Run proactive, recurring check-ins instead of waiting for tickets. For example, reach out a few weeks after go-live to review how their forms are performing
  • Use product usage data to spot clients who are not getting full value yet
  • Meet clients in person. Join us at clerk conferences and marketing events a few times a year. We cover all travel & lodging expenses

Spot opportunity

  • Tell clients about services they do not use yet (digital forms, payments, .gov domains, accessibility, training) without it feeling like a pitch
  • Flag possible expansion and renewal opportunities to the sales team

Training

  • Get clients to real proficiency with the product, not just past their immediate question
  • Work with Product Managers to co-host webinars about new features and training

Tools you will use: Intercom and Fin, Linear, Claude, our help center, screen recording, Zoom phone.

How we work

  • Delight over deflection. The goal is happy, successful clients, not fewer conversations
  • Ownership over routing. A hard case is yours until it is resolved
  • Diagnose before you escalate. A developer should never have to ask what the client actually saw
  • Documentation is the foundation everything else runs on, not an afterthought
  • Teaching over ticket-closing. Proficiency, not just an answer

Who you are

  • You like people, and it shows. Clerks are often not technical, sometimes stressed, and now and then upset. You pick up the phone gladly and leave them calmer than you found them
  • Hospitable by nature. A background in hospitality or another service-first field is a plus
  • You have done support somewhere known for it. The standard we have in mind is Basecamp: competent, calm, and trusted to make the call
  • Technically deep. You read the error, open the browser console and the network tab, check a DNS record, find your way around WordPress, and follow the trail into the code with Claude's help
  • At home with developers. You know what a good bug report contains and you have filed plenty
  • High autonomy. You decide, act, and report. You do not wait to be told
  • A clear, warm, precise writer, with clients and across teams
  • A natural teacher, patient with less technical users
  • Able to see the whole account, not just the ticket in front of you

Who you might be

  • Someone who worked the Genius Bar at an Apple Store and misses solving problems for a person, not a queue
  • Someone who learned support at a company known for it, such as Basecamp, Automattic, or Help Scout
  • A hotel or hospitality professional who moved into software and kept the instincts
  • A former municipal or deputy clerk who was always the one who figured out the software. You already know our clients' world
  • Or maybe none of these! If the rest of this page sounds like you, we certainly want to hear from you

This is not the job for you if

  • You would rather work a queue than talk to people
  • You find non-technical users frustrating
  • You want to hand a problem to a developer and move on
  • You need someone to tell you what to do next

Work style

  • Independent and ownership-driven. You do not need heavy oversight to perform
  • Comfortable wearing several hats across products and brands
  • Comfortable in a lean, documentation-first team
  • Proactive rather than reactive with accounts

What success looks like

  • Clients describe working with us as a great experience
  • No client has to ask who is handling their problem. They already know it is you
  • Issues you file get fixed without a developer asking for more detail
  • Tickets stop recurring, not just get answered
  • Help center articles created or improved every week, and Fin resolving more each month
  • Repeat questions turned into product fixes or automation
  • Expansion and renewals tied to the accounts you touch
  • Account relationships that are trusted, not just responsive
  • The rest of the team gets better because you are on it

Requirements

Experience

  • Five or more years in technical support or support engineering at a software company, working directly with engineers
  • An issue tracker used daily: Linear preferred, Jira or similar is fine
  • Intercom or similar support tooling, including work with an AI support agent
  • A knowledge base you wrote that other people relied on
  • AI tools such as Claude already part of your daily work
  • Nice to have: government or municipal software, WordPress-based websites, hospitality or other service-first work
  • Able to travel within the US a few times a year. Not required, but very helpful to understand our customers better.

How to apply

  1. Apply through Workable. You will answer two short questions in writing and record a two-minute Loom video teaching us one thing
  2. Complete the Culture Index survey. You can do it right after you apply. We only review candidates who have completed it
  3. Interview with our Head of Client Success
  4. Paid take-home exercise built from real client situations
  5. Conversation with our CTO and founder, including a short role-play call with a clerk who needs help
  6. Offer letter, if selected

Benefits

  • Salary of $85,000 to $105,000 a year, depending on experience
  • 20 paid vacation days, plus public holidays for your country of residence
  • Fully remote, working Central US hours
  • Internet stipend
  • Gym membership or wellness stipend

We do not offer a health plan or a 401(k) today. The salary range reflects that.

About the Role

As a Senior Instructional Designer,  you will join Chime’s Operations and Member Experience Learning & Development team to design highly engaging, interactive, and modern learning strategies and experiences for our agents across our BPOs. You will apply your knowledge of adult learning methodologies to drive business outcomes through the development of a broad range of innovative learning solutions (e.g. instructor-led, virtual instructor-led, digital, self-paced, micro-learning, social learning) that promote transfer, retention, and application. You are a creative and analytical problem solver, and you have a passion for customer service. 

Your work - execution and continuous improvement - will impact thousands of BPO employees and millions of Chime members. This role requires someone who thrives in a flat, fast-moving organization using lightweight processes, creative ideas, and quick iteration to make a significant impact. 

In this role, you can expect to

  • Analyze and apply trends and standard methodologies in instructional design and learning technologies to continue to elevate all agents' learning experiences.

  • You have an eye for design, a serious obsession with learning and a proven ability to tie learning events to measurable outcomes that reflect our mission and culture.
